REGISTRY
137, Pekin Road.
SHANGHAI, 29th December, 1937.

MOL: 1.
Major R. E. Bourne,
Deputy Commissioner,
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

Dear Major Bourne,

Herewith is a copy of the translation of a letter
from me to the Editor of the Hwa Pei Wan Pao.

It is a pity that newspapers do not generally make
enquiries with reasonable diligence as to the authenticity of news
concerning private individuals before publishing it. The present
case is one in point: some organization is said to be in course of
being formed and certain persons are said to be interested in the
organization. It is said that I am one of these persons, whereas
in truth and in fact I have never played any part therein. If the
newspaper concerned had merely telephoned to me, it would have cer-
tainly had no difficulty whatsoever in ascertaining that I had no
connection whatever with the said organization. Since all news-
papers in Shanghai have practically been registered with the Municip-
al Police as a condition precedent to their publication, it would,
in my opinion, be quite in conformity with the Council's policy of
protecting public interests to give the newspapers a warning that
whenever responsible residents in the Settlement are mentioned as
being concerned with any organization, either of a political or of
a civic character, enquiries should first be made with reasonable
diligence as to the truth of such information before publishing it.

I am,
Yours truly,
（签名）

北京路137号。
上海，1937年12月29日。

MOL: 1.
R. E. Bourne 少校，
副总监，
上海公共租界工部局警务处。

亲爱的 Bourne 少校：

兹附上我致《华北晚报》编辑的一封信的译本副本。

遗憾的是，报纸在刊登涉及私人的新闻之前，通常未能以合理的勤勉态度核实其真实性。本案即为一例：据称某组织正在组建中，且某些人对该组织感兴趣。据说我是这些人之一，而事实上我从未在其中扮演任何角色。如果相关报社 merely 给我打个电话，就肯定能毫不费力地查明我与该所谓组织毫无关联。鉴于上海所有报纸实际上都已向工部局警务处注册，以此作为出版的前提条件，我认为，为了符合工部局保护公众利益的政策，应当向各报发出警告：每当提及租界内负责居民参与任何政治或 civic 性质的组织时，在刊登之前应先以合理的勤勉态度核实此类信息的真实性。

此致，
敬礼，
（签名）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Moh Wei Yuen ( 穆緯源 )
native of Ningpo, Chekiang taken by me D.S. Pitts
at S.B., Hdqrs. on the 15/5/38 and interpreted by Clerk Wong Chia-tsing

My name is Moh Wei Yuen, aged 39, native of
Ningpo and at present residing at House 5, Lane 411 Bubbling
Well Road.

From 1932 until the outbreak of the hostilities in
Shanghai last summer, I carried on business under the name
of the Wei Zung ( 緯成 ) Iron Works at 680 Dalny Road. When
the fighting commenced in the Eastern and Northern areas
I was forced to evacuate my factory, all my goods and
machinery being left there.

On February 7, 1938, I applied to the Shanghai
Citizens' Society for a pass that would enable me to have
my machinery removed south of the Soochow Creek. Although
this machinery was worth not more than $7,000, the Society
first assessed its value as being $30,000 but following
protracted negotiations, reduced this figure to $15,000.
The application was eventually approved on March 2, when
I paid the Shanghai Citizens' Society $1,500 in cash - a
fee equivalent to 10% of the assessed value of the goods.

The machinery was removed by truck on March 4, 1938,
to a godown at 691 Gordon Road, where it is being stored
awaiting to be sold.

I have no receipt for the money paid or any other
documents to prove this statement since all papers were
handed back to the Society in accordance with its
regulations.

This is my true statement.
(Signed) Moh Wei Yuen.

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
警方调查报告。

以下为浙江宁波籍人士穆緯源 ( Moh Wei Yuen ) 的陈述，由本人 D.S. Pitts 于1938年5月15日在特务科总部录取，并由职员 Wong Chia-tsing 翻译。

我叫穆緯源，39岁，宁波人，现居住于静安寺路411弄5号。

从1932年到去年夏天上海战事爆发前，我在大连路680号以“緯成”铁工厂的名义经营业务。当东部和北部地区开始战斗时，我被迫撤离工厂，所有的货物和机器都留在那里。

1938年2月7日，我向上海市民协会申请通行证，以便将我的机器运至苏州河以南。虽然这些机器的价值不超过7,000美元，但该协会最初估价为30,000美元，经过长期谈判后，将这一数字降至15,000美元。申请最终于3月2日获得批准，当时我以现金支付给上海市民协会1,500美元——这笔费用相当于货物评估价值的10%。

机器于1938年3月4日用卡车运至戈登路691号的仓库，目前储存在那里等待出售。

我没有收到付款收据或任何其他文件来证明这一陈述，因为根据该协会的规定，所有文件都已交回给协会。

这是我的真实陈述。
（签名）穆緯源。

Date May 7, 1938.
Subject (in full) The "Sao Tang Pao" (掃蕩報) published in Hankow.

Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse Liang Forwarded by C. Crawford. L. J.

The "Sao Tang Pao," which is one of the vernacular
papers published in Hankow, is the mouth-piece of the
Chinese Military. It is under the direction of General
Chen Cheng (陳誠), Garrison Commander of Hankow and
Wuchang, and has at present a circulation of 100,000 per
day as compared with 50,000 per day prior to the outbreak
of the Sino-Japanese hostilities.

Reports and comments of this paper are often found
reproduced in various local newspapers but the paper itself
cannot be bought in Shanghai and efforts to obtain the
copy mentioned in the attached translation have been
unsuccessful.

D.C. (CRIME)

April 21, 1938. Afternoon Translation.

Life Daily News and other local newspapers :-

THE ASSASSINATION OF YANG SING-TSUNG

Upon the withdrawal of Chinese troops from
Shanghai, Yang Sing-tsung (楊心正), alias Yang Foh-yuan
(楊福源), the former Chief of the Zau Woo Kyung
Merchants' Volunteer Corps, residing at No. 22 Tsing Zung
Li (親仁里) (Lane 2117), Avenue Haig, formed a Citizens'
Society with Koo Shing-ih (顧馨一) and about twenty
others. On January 21 Yang was assassinated near his
home.

In connection with this case, the French Police
last month arrested a person named Chu Ah-ming (朱阿明)
and his sweetheart Chu Chu Sz (朱朱氏). In his
statement Chu Ah-ming said that Kuo Tih-fu (郭鉄夫)
and Chang Ming-dah (張明達), who had been sentenced
by the Shanghai Second Special District Court for being
in possession of arms, were the principals in the murder.
The Police thereupon removed these two prisoners, as well
as a convict named Ying Kai-sung (尹開声), for
questioning. The Police later found that Kuo Tih-fu
and Chang Ming-dah were actually the principal offenders,
while Chu Ah-ming was an accessory. The other two
persons, Chu Chu Sz and Ying Kai-sung, had nothing to do
with the case.

Yesterday afternoon Kuo, Cheng and Chu were
charged under Article 271 of the Chinese Criminal Code in
the Shanghai Second Special District Court. Chang Ming-
dah did not appear as he was sick.

Questioned by the Judge as to why he had
assassinated Yang Sing-tsung, Kuo Tih-fu said: "Your
honour will find the reason in the 'Sao Tang Pao' (掃蕩報)
published in Hankow. It was clearly stated in that
paper that Yang Sing-tsung and many others had been
sentenced to death. We killed Yang in the interests of
the country and the people. Our superior officer had
ordered Chang Ming-dah to carry out the assassination, but
as he failed to do it for a long time, our superior
officer suspected him of conspiring with the enemy and
instructed me to watch him. On the day before the
assassination, I carried a pistol and Chang Ming-dah
carried a mauser pistol to the home of Chu Ah-ming, who
lived in the same alleyway as Yang Sing-tsung. On the
following day we took the arms from the home of Chu Ah-
ming. Chang Ming-dah killed Yang Sing-tsung with his
mauser pistol. Seeing that our object had been achieved,
I returned without firing a shot. We were living at No.
36 Chien Nyieh Li (建業里), Route Frelupt, and were
arrested on January 28 whilst doing certain work. I was
later sentenced to three months' imprisonment by this
Court."

Chu Ah-ming stated that he dared not warn
Yang Sing-tsung of the plot against his life because he had
been intimidated by Chang Ming-dah.

The case was remanded to April 27.

刑事处副总监

1938年4月21日。下午译文。

《生活日报》及其他本地报纸：-

杨心正遇刺案

中国军队撤出上海后，原兆丰洋行商团团长、居住在海格路亲仁里（2117弄）22号的杨心正 (Yang Sing-tsung)，又名杨福源 (Yang Foh-yuan)，与顾馨一 (Koo Shing-ih) 等约二十人组建了一个市民协会。1月21日，杨在家附近遇刺身亡。

与此案有关，法国警察上月逮捕了一名名叫朱阿明 (Chu Ah-ming) 的人及其情妇朱朱氏 (Chu Chu Sz)。朱阿明在供词中说，郭鉄夫 (Kuo Tih-fu) 和张明达 (Chang Ming-dah) 是谋杀案的主犯，二人曾因持有武器被上海第二特区法院判刑。警方随后提审了这两名囚犯以及一名名叫尹開声 (Ying Kai-sung) 的罪犯。警方后来发现，郭鉄夫和张明达确实是主犯，而朱阿明是从犯。另外两人，朱朱氏和尹開声，与本案无关。

昨天下午，郭、张和朱在上海第二特区法院被依据《中华民国刑法》第271条起诉。张明达因病未出庭。

法官询问郭鉄夫为何刺杀杨心正时，郭说：“阁下可以在汉口出版的《掃蕩報》中找到原因。该报明确指出，杨心正及许多人已被判处死刑。我们为了国家和人民的利益杀死了杨。我们的上级命令张明达执行刺杀，但由于他长时间未能执行，我们的上级怀疑他与敌人勾结，并指示我监视他。在刺杀的前一天，我携带一把手枪，张明达携带一把毛瑟手枪，前往与杨心正住在同一条弄堂的朱阿明家。第二天，我们从朱阿明家取出武器。张明达用他的毛瑟手枪杀死了杨心正。看到我们的目的已经达到，我一枪未发便返回了。我们居住在法租界建业里36号，1月28日我们在做某些工作时被捕。后来我被本院判处三个月监禁。”

朱阿明陈述说，他不敢警告杨心正有人策划谋害他的生命，因为他受到张明达的恐吓。

案件延期至4月27日审理。

Subject Complaint made by one named Mr. F. Shue re the removal of his
furniture etc from House No. 271 Chaoufoong Road.

Made by D.S. Eynstone. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

At 11.50 a.m. 30.4.38 one named Mr. F. Shue (Chinese
Citizen) employed in the accountant dept. of the British
American tobacco Co. Whashing Road and at present residing
in House No. 29 Dah Ching Li off Nanking Road visited Wayside
Police Station and made the following complaint against the
Shanghai Citizens Society Federation situated in the Yokohama Specie
Bank No. 24 The Bund the details being as follows:-

Mr. F. Shue's permanent residence is situated at No. 271
Chaoufoong Road he having vacated these premises owing to the
Sino Japanese Hostilities, failing to remove any of his
furnitures or personal belongings.

In effort to recover his property Mr. F. Shue reports
having paid several visits to the Shanghai Citizens Society Federation
situated in Yokohama Specie Bank in endeavour to obtain a pass
but the officials therein demanded $1,000.00.

Mr. F: Shue request that his complaint be brought to the
notice of Headquarters therefore this report is accordingly
forwarded.

The names of the individuals employed in the Shanghai
Society
Citizens Association who demanded the $1,000.00 are not known.

[Signature]

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Hongkew Station,
REPORT
Date April 12, 19 38.
Subject Dinner Party was held at the Japanese Club by the Shanghai
Citizens' Association.
Made by D. S. I. Watanabe. Forwarded by Barry a
Sir,
I have to report that the dinner party given by the
Shanghai Citizens' Special Association on the evening of April 12th
in honour of the high officials of the Reformed Government
of China was held at the Japanese Club without any incident
occurring.
Approximately some 200 guests attended amongst whom were
many government officials, military, naval officers, Consular
officials and civil personages.
The function commenced at 6.45 p.m. and concluded at
10 p.m. during which time Uniform Police and Detectives from
this station were on duty in the vicinity.
I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
Watanabe
D. S. I.

Subject "Shanghai Citizens' Society" - activities

Made by D.S. Pitts Forwarded by C. Craufurd D.

The "Shanghai Citizens' Society" situated in Room 49,
4th floor, Yokohama Specie Bank Building, 24 The Bund, has
two departments - Transportation and Relief Departments.
The Transportation Department has a monopoly in the
transporting of merchandise in war affected areas in Shanghai,
and the Society derives its income in the form of 10% of the
value (assessed by the Department) of the cargo transported.
After meeting its expenses, the Society will apply any
surplus monies towards the relief of refugees by the Relief
Department. Owing to the many difficulties encountered and
because of the fact that the Society is permitted to transport
merchandise in Hongkew District and Chapei, where the Japanese
Naval Landing Party, by which the Society is supported, holds
sway, the Society has been able so far to secure a total sum
of $15,000 which is only sufficient to pay the expenses of
the Society.
As no money is available for the Relief Department
to conduct charitable work, the Department is only engaged
in issuing blank application forms to former residents of the
Hongkew district and Chapei. Up to date, a total of 26,000
blank application forms have been distributed, but only
2,000 applicants have obtained residence passes.
The Society is now launching a membership campaign.
Persons who wish to join the Society must be recommended
by two committee members of the organization and the
privileges enjoyed by the members consist only of receiving
passes to the Hongkew district and Chapei. About 300 persons

March 11, 1938.
Afternoon Translation.

Shanghai Daily News (上海日報), a mosquito paper :-

NANTAO MAINTENANCE ASSOCIATION CEASES FUNCTIONING

Besides the 30,000 refugees housed in the 140 refugee camps in the Refugee Zone at Nantao, there are in Nantao some 100,000 residents, of whom 30,000 are finding it difficult to make a living and are being supplied with food by the Refugee Zone General Office. As regards the food supplies to the remaining 70,000 residents, one Nien (任) used to undertake purchases from the Foreign Settlements for transportation to the Refugee Zone with the permission of Father Jacquinot. However, following complaints from one Sung Sin-wu (沈心武) that Nien is monopolizing the market, Father Jacquinot has stopped Nien's enterprise and replaced him with Sung Sin-wu.

Subsequently, Sung Sin-wu formed a so-called "Merchants' Association" and daily transported large quantities of food supplies into Nantao. He levied heavy taxes on goods belonging to members of the Association, and this caused a heavy increase in the prices, to the disadvantage of the residents. Father Jacquinot wanted to interfere but found it impossible to do so, because Sung was in possession of a special pass which he had obtained after paying bribes to various quarters.

Upon learning of Sung's malpractices, Yao Ts-hsi (姚子胥) (Manager of the Pan Sung Yuen Garden 半淞園), who is a member of the Nantao Autonomous Committee, immediately proposed the suppression of the "Merchants' Association". Chen Yuin (陳云), Chairman, and Ling Chi-tan (凌季潭), Vice Chairman, of the "Autonomous Committee" supported the proposal and issued an order for its suppression, but this had no effect owing to the big influence enjoyed by Sung Sin-wu.

Unexpectedly, on March 9 when Sung Sin-wu was at work at the "Merchants' Association" three Japanese gendarmes came and drove him out of the premises. Since then, the whereabouts of Sung Sin-wu is unknown and the "Merchants' Association" has ceased functioning.

Ta Mei Wan Pao Morning Edition publishes the following articles:-

THE "JAPANESE SPIRIT"

In the eyes of the Chinese, the so-called "Japanese spirit" means "invasion". Now there is a new explanation of this expression. It is said that "Japanese spirit" means this: "If one wants to fight, one must do it in a proper manner; no attacks should be made without an advance warning". This explanation is promoted by Mr. Isoc Abe, leader of the Nippon Shakei Taishuto.

Recently, four desperadoes knocked at Mr. Abe's door and when he opened it, he was attacked and injured. After the affair, Mr. Abe made the following statement to newspapermen:- "The desperadoes are not well versed with the Japanese spirit. In Japan, if one wants to fight, one must do so in a proper manner".

《上海日报》（Shanghai Daily News），一家微不足道的小报：-

南市维持会停止运作

除了安置在南市难民区140个难民营中的30,000名难民外，南市还有约100,000名居民，其中30,000人生活困难，正由难民区总办事处供应食物。至于其余70,000名居民的食物供应，一位姓任（Nien）的人过去在饶家驹神父（Father Jacquinot）的许可下，负责从外国租界采购并运往难民区。然而，在沈心武（Sung Sin-wu）投诉任氏垄断市场后，饶家驹神父停止了任氏的业务，并改由沈心武接替。

随后，沈心武组建了一个所谓的“商人协会”，每天向南市运送大量食品物资。他对协会成员的货物征收重税，导致物价大幅上涨，损害了居民的利益。饶家驹神父试图干预，但发现无法做到，因为沈心武通过向各方行贿获得了一张特别通行证。

南市自治委员会成员、半淞园（Pan Sung Yuen Garden）经理姚子胥（Yao Ts-hsi）得知沈氏的不法行为后，立即提议取缔该“商人协会”。自治委员会主席陈云（Chen Yuin）和副主席凌季潭（Ling Chi-tan）支持该提议并发布取缔令，但由于沈心武势力庞大，此举未能见效。

出乎意料的是，3月9日，当沈心武在“商人协会”办公时，三名日本宪兵前来将其驱离场所。此后，沈心武下落不明，“商人协会”已停止运作。

《大美晚报》晨刊刊登以下文章：-

“日本精神”

在中国人眼中，所谓的“日本精神”意味着“侵略”。现在对这一表述有了新的解释。据说，“日本精神”意味着：“如果要打架，必须以正当方式进行；不得在没有预先警告的情况下发动攻击”。这一解释由日本社会大众党（Nippon Shakei Taishuto）领袖阿部矶男（Isoc Abe，音译）先生提倡。

最近，四名暴徒敲开阿部先生的门，当他开门时，遭到袭击并受伤。事后，阿部先生向记者发表如下声明：“这些暴徒并不精通日本精神。在日本，如果要打架，必须以正当方式进行”。

Mr. Vung Seu,

You are one of our dear fellow country men of China. You have gained
a handsome fortune at the King an race course and from speculation. Since
you have been rich, why are you greedy for a high position in the organiza-

Mr. Chu, since you have solved your problem of living do not act as
a puppet under the control of Japanese and to be called a traitor. You

Were China once conquered, you will be unavoidable to be a slave
without a nation. Although you can be an exception under the protection

Wake up Mr. Chu! Wake up Mr. Chu! You realize that a traitor never

(1) Don't support Japanese and co-operate with them.
(2) Don't give assistance to Japanese in forming any organization and

Mr. Chu, don't you know or hear of that somebody intends to adopt
drastic measures in dealing with you?

As well as Yue Chyoh Sung, a traitor, he will be dealt with so
severely as you.
To represent our view of patriotism; now just ask yourself:
Who are your enemies who destroyed

Date February 21, 19 38.
Subject The Shanghai Citizens Association.
Made by and Forwarded by Inspector Papp.

The Shanghai Citizens Association is an organization composed of a number of Chinese businessmen. It was established by the Japanese Authorities, after their occupation of the city, as a medium for the control of the Chinese masses. It is designed to take the place of the defunct General Chamber of Commerce of Greater Shanghai. Generally speaking, this organization is intended to function like the so-called "Peace Preservation Committee"(治安維持會), a puppet regime of a provisional nature established by the Japanese Authorities in every city under their military occupation.

The main objects of the Association, as proclaimed, are threefold:- (1) The restoration of agricultural and industrial conditions to normal; (2) The restoration of communication systems between Shanghai and other parts of the country; and (3) The transportation and distribution of daily necessities such as foodstuffs, fuel, etc. In addition to the above, this organization was also supposed to carry on relief work among war victims and refugees.

It is learned that about 120 local Chinese businessmen participated in the Association and twenty-one of them were elected as members of the various committees. They are Mr. Yao Mu-lien, General Manager of the Water Works Co. of Nantao; Mr. Koo Hsin Yi, Chairman of the Foodstuffs Merchant Union; Mr. Yung Chung Ching, General Manager of the Sheng Sin Weaving Co, and the Fu Sin Flour Co.; the late Mr. Loh Pah Hung, General Manager of the Nantao Power Co.; Mr. Chu I Chai (祝伊才), Chief Director of Yangchung(揚中) Power Co. of Changchow (常州); Mr. Yu Chu Sun(尤菊蓀), General Manager of the Cheng Hwa Weaving Co.; Mr. Chow Wen Sui(周文瑞).

上海市民协会是一个由多名中国商人组成的组织。它是在日军占领城市后，由日本当局建立的，作为控制中国民众的媒介。旨在取代已解散的大上海总商会。一般而言，该组织 intended to function 类似于所谓的“治安维持会”，这是日本当局在其军事占领的每个城市建立的临时性傀儡政权。

该协会宣称的主要目标有三：- (1) 恢复农业和工业状况至正常水平；(2) 恢复上海与国内其他地区的交通系统；以及 (3) 运输和分配食品、燃料等日常必需品。除上述内容外，该组织还 supposed to 开展针对战争受害者和难民的救济工作。

据悉，约有120名本地中国商人参与了该协会，其中21人当选为各委员会委员。他们是：南市自来水公司总经理姚慕莲（Yao Mu-lien）先生；食品商公会主席顾辛夷（Koo Hsin Yi，音译）先生；盛新织造厂和福新面粉公司总经理荣钟敬（Yung Chung Ching，音译）先生；已故的南市电力公司总经理罗柏洪（Loh Pah Hung，音译）先生；常州扬中电力公司总董事祝伊才（Chu I Chai）先生；成华织造公司总经理尤菊孙（Yu Chu Sun）先生；周文瑞（Chow Wen Sui）先生。

Date February 17 19 38.

Subject Communist circular received through the Post by Shanghai Citizens'
Association, No. 24 The Bund, on 10.2.38.
Made by D.I. Kuh Pao Hwa Forwarded by C Crawford D.I.

In compliance with the instructions of D.C. (Special
Branch) on the attached file, I have to report that discreet
enquiries have as yet failed to confirm the Communist source
of the circular which was sent to the Shanghai Citizens'
Association on February 10, 1938.

A careful examination of the document shows that
it lacks both the calligraphical style as well as the
phraseology common to the Chinese Communists. In many parts
also, the ideology of the author is expressed more in the
terms of the story-teller than of the Communists. Neither
can it be stated that the literature emanates from the
Chinese Trotsky Clique, the members of which are suspected
to be pro-Japanese in their sentiments.

With reference to the threatening-letter file.
attached (flagged), a comparison has been made of the
calligraphy of both documents in the office of Clerk
May Yoh, Crime Branch Headquarters. Although the afore-
mentioned circular was originally written with a stencil-
pencil, while the threatening letter was written with a
Chinese pen-brush, there is every resemblance in the
penmanship on the two documents.

Kuh Pao hwa

遵照附卷中副总监（特别处）的指示，本人谨此报告，经谨慎调查，迄今未能证实1938年2月10日发送给上海市民协会的传单来自共产主义方面。

仔细检查该文件显示，它既缺乏中国共产党人常见的书法风格，也缺乏其常用措辞。在许多部分，作者的意识形态表达更类似于说书人的口吻，而非共产党人的风格。也不能断定该文献出自中国托洛茨基派系，尽管该派系成员被怀疑持有亲日情绪。

关于所附（标记的）恐吓信档案，已在刑事侦缉处总部梅约（May Yoh）书记员的办公室对两份文件的笔迹进行了比对。虽然上述传单最初是用蜡纸铅笔书写的，而恐吓信是用毛笔书写的，但两份文件在笔迹上极为相似。

At 5p.m. on the 12-2-38, a report was made by
the Shanghai Citizens Association to the Central
Station to the effect that the association had
received a letter containing a pamphlet issued by the
Chinese Communist Party and threatening to the work of
the association.

Enquiries were made by the detectives and the
report is now the subject of No. 184/38 Central
Station.

During the course of enquiries, Mr. Dou Sho Chi
(周孝智) secretary, employed by the Shanghai Citizens
Association was interviewed, and stated that prior to
receiving the letter containing the printed communistic
pamphlet, on the 30-1-38, the association had received
a registered letter from "The Chinese Iron Blood
Traitor Elimination Corps" the contents of which were
also of a threatening nature, to the effect that the
lives of the members of the association were in danger
This letter was handed over to the police and it was
requested that further enquiries to be made regarding
same, by the Police.

The Shanghai Citizens Association was established
at Room Nos. 48, 49 and 50, in the building of the
Yokohama Specie Bank, No. 24, The Bund on or about
24-1-38.

The task of the association so far as can be
ascertained is to obtain passes from the Japanese
Authorities for the Chinese residents who wish to
return to their homes in the north of the Soochow
Creek, and the removal of their property from the war

1938年2月12日下午5时，上海市民协会向中央巡捕房报案，称该协会收到一封信，内含中国共产党发行的小册子，并对协会的工作构成威胁。

侦探进行了调查，该报告现为中央巡捕房第184/38号案件的主题。

在调查过程中，讯问了上海市民协会聘用的秘书陶舒池（原文此处中文名写作周孝智，但拼音为Dou Sho Chi，结合上下文及后文统一译为陶舒池）先生，他表示在收到含有印刷共产主义小册子的信件之前，即1938年1月30日，协会曾收到一封来自“中华铁血锄奸团”的挂号信，内容同样具有威胁性，称协会成员的生命处于危险之中。该信已移交警方，并要求警方对此进行进一步调查。

上海市民协会于1938年1月24日左右在外滩24号横滨正金银行大楼的48、49和50室成立。

Loh Pah Hung was killed not long ago. You are not afraid to meet
death trying to organize the so called Citizen Association. As your
office is situated in the upstairs of the Yokohama Specie Bank, you think
you will have no worry to work under under the protection of the
Imperialistic organization. You must understand that the bullet goes
through wherever it likes, the lives of shameless people like you will be
endangered sooner or later, even if you hide yourselves wherever you choose
as best. You are tempted by money to work in a such kind of organization,
but you are under the observation of us - the Hot Blood patriots. Can you
save your life without danger ? Here we give you this warning first and
let you have a happy Chinese New Year. You must consider the matter during
these few days. If you are able to reform yourselves, an announcement
must be inserted in the newspapers regarding the puppet Citizens Associa-
tion, otherwise you will be treated similiar to the late Loh Pah Hung.
Our action must be adopted following this warning.

罗柏鸿不久前被杀。你们不怕死，试图组织所谓的市民协会。由于你们的办公室设在横滨正金银行楼上，你们以为在帝国主义组织的保护下工作可以高枕无忧。你们必须明白，子弹随心所欲地穿透一切，像你们这样无耻之徒的生命迟早会面临危险，即使你们躲藏在自以为最好的地方。你们受金钱诱惑在这种组织中工作，但你们正处于我们——热血爱国者的监视之下。你们能保全性命而不遇危险吗？在此我们先给予警告，并祝你们春节快乐。你们必须在这几天内考虑此事。如果你们能够改过自新，必须在报纸上刊登关于傀儡市民协会的声明，否则你们将受到与已故罗柏鸿相同的待遇。

A printed pamphlet issued by the Chinese Communist Party received at the Shanghai Citizens Association located at No.24 The Bund on 10-2-38.

Major E. . . Bourne,
Deputy Commissioner,
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
----------

Dear Major Bourne,

I have to thank you for the translation which you were good enough to have made of the correction which the "Hwa Mei Wan Pao" published in its issue for the 7th instant. Although in the correction an apology is tendered to me, nevertheless, the inclusion in the article of my name when the original text contains not the slightest reference to it cannot but be an act clearly prompted by malice. For the moment, I have no desire to take further action in the matter, but I think that in the best interest of public peace the Police might consider it desirable to warn that Paper that it should in future use every reasonable diligence in ascertaining the truth of any information concerning local residents of responsibility which might be intended for publication.

If, as I have said before, that Paper had from the start inquired of me if I had associated myself with the so-called Shanghai Citizens Association, I would have repudiated the allegation and considerable amount of embarrassment and trouble would have been avoided.

The correction so promptly made by that Paper is an eloquent testimonial to the efficiency of the Special Branch under your able command and the effective control exercised by the Police

感谢您惠予翻译《华美晚报》在本月7日刊出的更正声明。虽然在该更正中向我致歉，然而，原文中丝毫未提及我的名字，文章中却列入我的姓名，这显然是一种出于恶意的行为。暂时我无意就此采取进一步行动，但我认为，为了公众安宁的最大利益，警方或许可以考虑警告该报，今后在刊登有关当地负责任居民的任何信息前，应尽一切合理的努力核实真相。

The "Hwa Mei Wan Pao" (華美晚報) publishes the
following correction on February 7, 1938 :-

A CORRECTION

On February 1 this paper published a translation
of an article entitled "Big Events in China's Extensive
War of Resistance", in which it was stated: "According to
a Japanese report, the 'Shanghai Citizens' Society'
supported by some 100 Chinese leaders will be established
soon". Later it was found that the translator had
included the name of Mr. Feng Ping-nan (馮炳南) in the
translation although the original English text, which
was taken from the "China Weekly Review", makes no mention
of Mr. Feng.

Fearing misunderstanding, this paper hereby
publishes this correction and tenders an apology to
Mr.Feng Pingnan.
page_data.zh:
《华美晚报》于 1938 年 2 月 7 日刊登以下更正声明：-

更正声明

本报于 2 月 1 日刊登了一篇题为《中国全面抗战中的重大事件》的文章译文，其中称：“据日本报道，由约 100 名中国领袖支持的‘上海市民协会’即将成立”。后发现译者在译文中加入了冯炳南（Feng Ping-nan）先生的名字，尽管取自《密勒氏评论报》的英文原文中并未提及冯先生。

为避免误解，本报特此刊登此更正声明，并向冯炳南先生致歉。

page_data.en:
High Prices of
Coal Justified,
State Dealers

Considerable Increase in
Expenses

POOTUNG COAL "RACKET"
IS EXPOSED

Coal prices in Shanghai have increased by from 80 to 100 per cent. during the past year or so, it was learned yesterday by the "North-China Daily News" from reliable sources. All qualities of coal have been affected by this phenomenal rise in prices, which has given rise to charges of profiteering against local coal dealers. It was pointed out yesterday that the price of fuel oil has shown an increase of only 10 per cent. during the same period, which left an increase of about 70 per cent. to be accounted for by Shanghai coal merchants.

Several reasons for the heavy rise in prices were put forward by local coal firms yesterday when questioned on the subject by the "North-China Daily News." The manager of one coal company pointed out that freight charges had increased by over 100 per cent., and in addition it was difficult to obtain wharfage accommodation. The practice before the local "war" was to land the coal on the Pootung side, store it there, and then to bring it over to the Shanghai side as required. In view of the fact that the Japanese are in occupation of Pootung, it is now necessary to land the coal at a wharf on the Shanghai side, transport it in lorries to a coal yard in the Settlement, and then deliver it as required, which means using more lorries. Charges for the hire of lorries have increased, and an extra charge is the maintenance of a coal yard in Shanghai. Charges for coolie hire have also increased, the daily wage being one dollar as against 30 cents before the "war."

There definitely is a coal shortage in Shanghai, the coal merchant interviewed emphatically stated. The majority of the coal mines in the Yangtze Valley have been closed up as a result of the hostilities, and the quantities of coal brought in from other sources do not cover the demand. The coal merchant, who stated that he supplied 50 per cent. of the demand from the Shanghai market, pointed out that the anthracite coal sold by his firm was the only anthracite obtainable in Shanghai.

Contributing to the coal shortage, he stated, was the fact that about 120,000 tons of coal were stored over in Pootung, and could not be brought over to Shanghai by the owners, consisting mostly of Chinese companies. The Japanese, said the merchant, refused to give their permission for the coal to be removed. The coal had been stored over in Pootung before the war, and only small quantities had been "rescued" by the coal firms since the outbreak of hostilities. The merchant denied that the shortage of coal was responsible for the heavy increase in prices, which, he claimed, was solely on account of heavier freight charges and other drawbacks.

Due to the failure of a large number of coal mines in the Yangtze Valley and in the North, the entire output of the local coal dealer was being used by the Shanghai Power Company, leaving a shortage in coal available for the general public.

"Racket" in Pootung

Sinister rumours of a "coal racket," which had been functioning until about two weeks ago, were imparted to the "North-China Daily News" by another coal dealer who was interviewed with regard to the rise in prices. Stolen coal was being brought over the Whangpoo and landed on the French Bund, to be distributed on the next day at cut-rate prices, by a Sino-Japanese "syndicate," according to the dealer.

The coal, he stated, almost certainly came from the large stock which is lying over in Pootung, and which cannot be touched by the rightful owners. Those responsible for the "racket," he stated, were probably Japanese and Chinese hooligans, who manage to evade the authorities and land the coal in Shanghai under the cover of darkness.

When the Chinese were in occupation of Pootung, the dealer stated, it was necessary to pay a substantial "squeeze" before coal could be brought across to Shanghai. With the Japanese in occupation, the coal cannot be brought across at all. The original reason given by the Japanese was that the Nantao boom prevented ships from coming down river, and, the coal being stored at a point above the boom, it could not be landed at Shanghai. With the removal of the boom, the Japanese are still refusing to allow the coal to be moved, as they will not permit ships carrying the coal to pass.

As a result of the refusal to allow the coal to be removed, Shanghai is putting up with quite a serious coal shortage, made worse by the fact that increased expenses have sent the price of coal to a high level. Meanwhile, it is rumoured that coal is being sold over in Pootung for as low as seven dollars per ton. This coal is also, presumably, taken from the large stocks which are stored on the Pootung side.

（批：D.S. Hoe 6/2 C 2/2）
page_data.zh:
煤价高涨有理，
商贩称

开支大幅增加

浦东煤炭“黑幕”
被揭露

据《字林西报》昨日从可靠消息源获悉，在过去一年左右的时间里，上海的煤炭价格上涨了80%至100%。所有等级的煤炭都受到这一惊人涨幅的影响，这也引发了针对本地煤炭商人的囤积居奇指控。昨日有人指出，在同一时期，燃料油的价格仅上涨了10%，这意味着上海煤炭商人需对约70%的涨幅作出解释。

昨日，本地煤炭公司在接受《字林西报》就此事询问时，提出了价格大幅上涨的几个原因。一家煤炭公司的经理指出，运费已上涨超过100%，此外还难以获得码头停泊设施。在本地“战事”爆发前，惯例是将煤炭卸在浦东一侧，在那里储存，然后根据需要运至上海一侧。鉴于日军目前占领了浦东，现在必须将煤炭卸在上海一侧的码头，用卡车运至租界内的煤栈，然后再按需配送，这意味着需要使用更多的卡车。卡车租赁费用已经上涨，而在上海维持一个煤栈也是一项额外开支。苦力雇佣费用也有所增加，日工资为一元，而“战前”为三十美分。

受访的煤炭商人 emphatically 声明，上海确实存在煤炭短缺。由于战事影响，长江流域的大多数煤矿已经关闭，而从其他来源运入的煤炭数量无法满足需求。这位声称其供应占上海市场需求50%的商人指出，其公司销售的无烟煤是上海唯一能买到的无烟煤。

他称，加剧煤炭短缺的一个事实是，约有12万吨煤炭储存在浦东，而其所有者（大多为中国公司）无法将其运至上海。该商人说，日本人拒绝许可将这些煤炭移走。这些煤炭是在战前储存在浦东的，自敌对行动爆发以来，煤炭公司仅“抢救”出少量煤炭。该商人否认煤炭短缺是导致价格大幅上涨的原因，他声称价格上涨完全是因为运费加重和其他不利因素所致。

由于长江流域和华北的大量煤矿停产，本地煤炭经销商的全部产出正被上海电力公司（Shanghai Power Company）使用，导致供公众使用的煤炭出现短缺。

浦东的“黑幕”

另一位就价格上涨问题接受采访的煤炭商人向《字林西报》透露了一些关于一个直至约两周前仍在运作的“煤炭黑幕”的不祥谣言。据该商人称，一个中日“辛迪加”（syndicate）正将偷来的煤炭运过黄浦江，卸在外滩（French Bund），并于次日以低价分销。

他说，这些煤炭几乎可以肯定来自储存在浦东、合法所有者无法动用的大量库存。他说，负责这一“黑幕”的可能是日本和中国流氓，他们设法逃避当局监管，并在夜色掩护下将煤炭卸在上海。

该商人称，当中国人占领浦东时，在将煤炭运过江至上海之前，必须支付巨额的“勒索金”（squeeze）。随着日本人占领浦东，煤炭根本无法运过江。日本人最初给出的理由是，南市的拦江坝阻止船只顺流而下，而煤炭储存在拦江坝上游的地点，因此无法在上海卸货。随着拦江坝的移除，日本人仍然拒绝允许移动煤炭，因为他们不允许运载煤炭的船只通过。

由于拒绝允许移走煤炭，上海正忍受着相当严重的煤炭短缺，而费用的增加使煤价处于高位，进一步加剧了这一状况。与此同时，有传言称，浦东那边的煤炭售价低至每吨七元。据推测，这些煤炭也取自储存在浦东一侧的大量库存。

（批：D.S. Hoe 6/2 C 2/2）

日本人向

北部地区

日本海军部门签发

可以搬离

必须向上海市民协会
申请许可证

日本海军发言人昨晚宣布，重新向可能愿意返回家园的中国居民开放虹口和杨树浦地区，并公布了允许前中国居民返回的规定。
他说，此类人员必须通过上海市民协会，向日本海军特别调查科申请许可。
申请表将在位于横滨正金银行四楼的协会办公室提供。
他说，除其他所需信息外，申请人必须说明拟重新居住的房屋位置，经海军服务部门调查后将予以批准。

中国货物搬离
日本海军当局昨晚取消了禁止搬离虹口和杨树浦地区中国籍货物的禁令，并公布了允许此类货物移动的公共规定。此前，只有日本或外籍拥有的货物才被允许运往苏州河以南地区。
虽然日本人和第三国国民都需要向日本总领事馆提交货物转移申请，但中国人必须向上海市民协会提交申请。该机构在横滨正金银行四楼设有办公室。这些文件将转送海军特别服务科审批。
日本人和第三国国民的货物搬离许可证由总领事馆签发，中国人的则由海军特别服务科签发。

预定限制
一位发言人宣布，在搬离货物之前，必须向管辖货物所在地区的日本宪兵队出示这些许可证。他补充说，正如目前所做的那样，用于运输此类货物的车辆和工人数量限制将由日本居留地防卫团总部制定。
该发言人进一步表示，日本海军当局保留检查任何正在搬离的货物的权利。

（批：S.D. Hoeing 7/2 6 3/2）

Permits For Removal Of
Chinese Goods Available
Through Residents' Body

Documents Must Be Lodged With Citizens' Group,
With Application For Transfer Of Merchandise
Across Creek; Military Police Authority

OPENING OF HONGKEW AND YANGTZEPOO
TO CHINESE IS ANNOUNCED

Dropping the bars against the removal of Chinese-owned goods in the Hongkew and Yangtzepoo areas the Japanese naval authorities last night made public regulations under which such movements of merchandise would be permitted. Hitherto only Japanese or foreign-owned goods were allowed to be transported to areas south of Soochow Creek

While both Japanese and third-party nationals will be required to file applications for the transfer of merchandise to the Japanese Consulate-General, Chinese will have to present their's to the Shanghai Japanese Citizens' Association. This body has offices in the Yokohama Specie Bank, Fourth Floor. These documents will be forwarded to the Special Service Section of the Navy for approval.

Permits for the removal of goods will be issued by the Consulate-General in the case of Japanese and third-party nationals, and the Special Service Section of the Navy in the case of Chinese.

Military Authority

These permits will have to be presented to the Japanese military police station having jurisdiction over the district in which the goods are located before the latter are removed, a spokesman announced. Limitations regarding the number of vehicles and workmen used for the transportation of such merchandise will be made, as now, by the headquarters of the Japanese Settlement Defence Corps, he added. The Japanese naval authorities, the spokesman further stated, reserved the right to inspect any merchandise being removed.

Chinese Residence

Confirming recurrent reports of the impending reopening of Hongkew and Yangtzepoo areas to residence by Chinese, a Japanese naval spokesman last night announced rules under which former native residents of the districts would be permitted to return.

Chinese wishing to resume residence in the Hongkew and Yangtzepoo Districts, the spokesman said, would have to apply to the Special Service Section of the Japanese Navy, through the Shanghai Citizens' Association.

Office Of Issue

Special blanks for the purpose, he said, were available in the offices of the Association in the Yokohama Specie Bank, fourth floor. Required would be particulars regarding the location of the house to be reoccupied and other details.

Permission for residence and business would be granted by the Special Service Section of the Navy upon investigation, the spokesman stated.

The announcement that former Chinese residents of the northern areas will be allowed to return to their homes is looked upon as one of the most important developments locally in many a day.

It is much too early to tell just how far-reaching the effects of the change will be, while doubtless there will be some considerable complication in effecting the return of anything but a limited number of residents during the next few weeks.

One of the most encouraging aspects of the announcement, it is felt, is that the new scheme provides for the resumption of business and industry by Chinese in the area. The rehabilitation of the northern district will take an extremely long time, but the advent of a beginning is significant.

In an exclusive story published just one week ago, "The Shanghai Times" indicated that the return of Chinese to the northern area would be only a matter of days, although the method originally outlined was necessarily changed.

The first plan was to place the responsibility of issuing passes to former Chinese residents in the hands of the Shanghai Municipal Police, but this responsibility has now been handed over to the Japanese.

Doubt has been expressed as to the response which would be forthcoming with regard to any move to return former Chinese residents to the northern areas, but, on the other hand, it is felt that if adequate protection is provided, there will be no lack of response.

Those who have studied the situation believe that a great deal hinges upon the manner in which passes are issued and the reduction of red tape to a minimum, while it is also hoped that any unnecessary friction may be avoided.

Western Areas

Twenty-four hours after Chinese were freely admitted, third-party nationals regained access to extra-Settlement areas west of the railway yesterday morning.

Passes, which had hitherto been asked of foreigners entering the area, were no longer required. Japanese sentries remained on duty at the railway crossings, while small guard outposts also were maintained nearby.

A Japanese military spokesman last night confirmed that sentries no longer asked for passes at any of the posts along the western perimeter.

Horseback riders were much in evidence yesterday especially on Chungshan Road.

Unarmed policemen of the Ta Tao Government were also stationed near the railway crossings to examine Chinese entering or leaving Japanese-controlled territory.

华人货物搬迁许可证
可通过居民团体申领

文件须提交至市民团体，
申请将货物运过苏州河；军事警察当局

宣布向华人开放虹口与杨树浦

日本海军当局昨晚公布了相关规定，允许在虹口和杨树浦地区搬运华人所有的货物，从而取消了对该地区华人货物搬迁的禁令。此前，只有日籍或外籍所有的货物才被允许运往苏州河以南地区。

虽然日籍及第三国国民均需向日本总领事馆提交货物转运申请，但华人则须将其申请提交给上海日本人居留民团。该团体办公室位于横滨正金银行四楼。这些文件将转呈海军特务部审批。

日籍及第三国国民的货物搬迁许可证由总领事馆签发，华人的许可证则由海军特务部签发。

军事当局

一位发言人宣布，在货物搬离之前，必须向管辖货物所在地区的日本宪兵队出示这些许可证。他补充说，用于运输此类货物的车辆和工人数量限制，仍将像目前一样由日本居留民团防卫本部制定。该发言人进一步表示，日本海军当局保留检查任何被搬离货物的权利。

华人居住

一位日本海军发言人昨晚证实了关于虹口和杨树浦地区即将重新对华人开放居住的反复报道，并宣布了允许该地区前本地居民返回的规则。

该发言人称，希望恢复在虹口和杨树浦区居住的华人，必须通过上海市民协会向日本海军特务部提出申请。

签发机构

他说，为此目的专用的空白表格可在外滩横滨正金银行四楼的协会办公室索取。需要提供拟重新入住的房屋位置及其他细节。

该发言人表示，经调查后，海军特务部将批准居住和经商许可。

允许北部地区的前华人居民返回家园的这一公告，被视为当地多日来最重要的进展之一。

现在判断这一变化影响有多深远还为时过早，尽管毫无疑问，在未来几周内，除了有限数量的居民外，要实现更多居民的回归将会相当复杂。

人们认为，该公告最令人鼓舞的方面之一是，新方案规定华人可在该地区恢复商业和工业活动。北部地区的复兴将需要极长的时间，但迈出的第一步意义重大。

就在上周发表的一篇独家报道中，《上海泰晤士报》指出，华人返回北部地区只是几天内的事，尽管最初概述的方法必然发生了改变。

最初的计划是将向前华人居民签发通行证的责任交给上海公共租界工部局警务处，但这一责任现已移交给日方。

有人对针对让前华人居民返回北部地区的任何举措所能得到的响应表示怀疑，但另一方面，人们认为如果提供充分的保护，响应者不会少。

那些研究过局势的人认为，很大程度上取决于通行证的签发方式以及将繁文缛节减至最低限度，同时也希望避免任何不必要的摩擦。

西部区域

在华人被自由准入24小时后，第三国国民于昨天上午重新获得了进入铁路以西越界筑路区域的权限。

此前进入该区域的外国人被要求持有的通行证已不再需要。日本哨兵仍在铁路道口执勤，附近也设有小型警卫哨所。

一位日本军方发言人昨晚证实，哨兵不再在西侧周边任何哨所要求出示通行证。

昨天骑马者随处可见，尤其是在中山路上。

大道政府（Ta Tao Government）的无武装警察也驻扎在铁路道口附近，检查进出日本控制区的华人。

China Daily News (中國日報) :-
THE DECLINE OF TRADE IN SHANGHAI

China Daily News (中國日報) and other local newspapers :-

法国警察局第2219/S号报告译文，日期为1938年2月1日。
机密
主题：上海市民公会。

由于罗伯洪（LOH PAH HONG）先生于1937年12月30日遇刺身亡，上海市民公会的组织工作暂时中止。然而，根据某些消息，该协会正准备恢复活动。据说，罗伯洪先生和杨福源（YANG FU YUAN）（1月21日遇刺）留下的两个空缺职位，已由九江路20号“大仓洋行”进出口公司买办、住杰斐逊路64号的张理卿（CHANG LI CHING），以及四川路330号朝鲜银行董事、亦为孔茂垄断公司董事、住愚园路749弄71号的顾桂林（KOU FWEI LING），别名顾棣三（KOO DI SHAN）担任。（1月28日接受问询时，顾先生否认与该协会的组织有关联）。
据说该协会由五个部门组成，即：
1) 秘书处。
2) 总务处。
3) 会计处。
4) 运输处。

These five persons are said to have already concluded
an arrangement with Mitsubishi Shoji Kaisha, 36 Kiukiang
Road and Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, 185 Szechuen Road, and in
addition are reported to have organised a Committee for
the Supply of Coal, which will particularly deal with the
transportation of this commodity from Pootung to Shanghai.
On each ton transported to Shanghai, a tax of $2 will be
levied by the Committee, it is said.

The Shanghai Citizens' Civic Association published
a notice in the North-China Daily News of January 24, 1938
inviting business houses desiring to bring their coal from
Pootung to Shanghai to write to them direct.

During the course of enquiries we have secured the
home address of Mr. OU CHENG YONG (吴曾鎔), a member
of the Executive Committee of the Association. This
individual, alias OU YEU YU (吴友渔), Director of
the Liyang (Kiangsu) Electricity Company, has resided at
43 Edinburgh Terrace, Edinburgh Road since January 26, 1938.

According to certain information received, the Chinese
Authorities in Hankow are said to have issued warrants of
arrest against the twenty-one persons forming the Executive
Committee of the Shanghai Citizens' Civic Association. This
information, however, appears to be without foundation. It
is true that the Government Authorities are discontented
with the activities of these individuals, but up to the
present they have given no instructions to have them
arrested.

一名煤炭商人，已证明真正在为协会有效工作。

据说这五人已与九江路36号的三菱商事会社和四川路185号的三井物产会社达成协议，此外还据报道组织了一个煤炭供应委员会，专门处理从浦东到上海的煤炭运输事务。据说，每运抵上海一吨煤炭，委员会将征收2美元税款。

上海市民公会在1938年1月24日的《字林西报》上刊登了一则通知，邀请希望将煤炭从浦东运至上海的商号直接致函该会。

在调查过程中，我们获取了该协会执行委员会委员吴曾鎔（OU CHENG YONG）先生的家庭住址。此人别名吴友渔（OU YEU YU），江苏利阳电力公司董事，自1938年1月26日起居住在爱丁堡路爱丁堡公寓43号。

根据收到的某些消息，汉口中国当局据说已对组成上海市民公会执行委员会的21人发出逮捕令。然而，这一消息似乎毫无根据。确实，政府当局对这些人的活动感到不满，但截至目前，他们并未下达逮捕他们的指令。

Made by D.S. Hocking Forwarded by C. Crawford D.I.

With reference to the remarks of the D.C.
(Special Branch) on the attached file, further details
were obtained by members of the Special Branch on
visiting the premises located in the Yokohama Specie
Bank Building, 24 The Bund.

The Shanghai Citizens' Society, which came into
existence during the latter part of December, 1937,
with an office at Room 301, Shanghai Women's Bank Building,
Nanking Road, has been inactive since the assassination
of Mr. Loh Fah-hung, one of the leading committee members.
On January 21, 1938, the society established an office
in Room 49, 4th floor, Yokohama Specie Bank Building,
24 The Bund, and commenced functioning, more or less
under the control of the Japanese. Two Japanese
civilians appear to be posted at the entrance of Room 49.
According to Mr. Wu Ching-yung (吳錦鎔), Chief of the
Transportation Department, this society is the same as
that formerly located in the Shanghai Women's Bank Building,
Nanking Road, the internal organization being exactly
the same as before. The regulations of the society have
already been submitted to the Shanghai Municipal Council;
a further report regarding its functioning at the new
address will, according to Mr. Wu Ching-yung, be made
shortly to the S.M.C.

The committee members of the society are as
before with the exception of Mr. Chang Li-ching (張理卿)
alias Chang Zao-yuan (張肇源), ex-compradore of the
Okura Trading Co., 20 Kiukieng Road, and Mr. Koo Kwei-ling

上海市民协会于1937年12月下旬成立，原办公室设在南京路上海女子商业储蓄银行大楼301室。自该会主要委员之一罗发洪（音译）先生遇刺身亡以来，该会一直未开展活动。1938年1月21日，该会在外滩24号横滨正金银行大楼四楼49室设立办公室，并开始运作，其活动或多或少处于日本人的控制之下。两名日本平民似乎驻守在49室入口处。据运输部主任吴锦镛（吳錦鎔）先生称，该协会与原先设在南京路上海女子商业储蓄银行大楼的协会为同一组织，内部架构与之前完全相同。协会章程已提交给上海公共租界工部局；据吴锦镛先生称，不久将就其在新址的运作情况向工部局提交进一步报告。

Jan. 27, 38.

Shanghai Chinese Citizens' Society - details of
organization.

With reference to the remarks of the S.C.
(Special Branch) on the attached file, further details
were obtained by members of the Special Branch on
visiting the premises located in the Yokohama Specie
Bank Building, 24 The Bund.

The Shanghai Citizens' Society, which came into
existence during the latter part of December, 1937,
with an office at Room 301, Shanghai Women's Bank Building,
Nanking Road, has been inactive since the assassination
of Mr. Loh Fah-hung, one of the leading committee members.
On January 21, 1938, the society established an office
in Room 49, 4th floor, Yokohama Specie Bank Building,
24 The Bund, and commenced functioning, more or less
under the control of the Japanese. Two Japanese
civilians appear to be posted at the entrance of Room 49.
According to Mr. Wu Ching-yung (吴卿镛), Chief of the
Transportation Department, this society is the same as
that formerly located in the Shanghai Women's Bank Building,
Nanking Road, the internal organization being exactly
the same as before. The regulations of the society have
already been submitted to the Shanghai Municipal Council;
a further report regarding its functioning at the new
address will, according to Mr. Wu Ching-yung, be made
shortly to the S.M.C.

The committee members of the society are as
before with the exceptions of Mr. Chang Li-ching (张礼卿)
alias Chang Zao-yuan (张肇原), ex-compradore of the
Chare Trading Co., 20 Kiukiang Road, and Mr. Kao Kwei-ling

1938年1月27日。

上海市民协会——组织详情。

参照附卷中特别处秘书长的批注，特别处成员在走访位于外滩24号横滨正金银行大楼的办公地点后，获得了更多细节。

上海市民协会于1937年12月下旬成立，原办公室设在南京路上海女子商业储蓄银行大楼301室。自该会主要委员之一罗发洪（音译）先生遇刺身亡以来，该会一直未开展活动。1938年1月21日，该会在外滩24号横滨正金银行大楼四楼49室设立办公室，并开始运作，其活动或多或少处于日本人的控制之下。两名日本平民似乎驻守在49室入口处。据运输部主任吴卿镛（吴卿镛）先生称，该协会与原先设在南京路上海女子商业储蓄银行大楼的协会为同一组织，内部架构与之前完全相同。协会章程已提交给上海公共租界工部局；据吴卿镛先生称，不久将就其在新址的运作情况向工部局提交进一步报告。

relief to residents in war affected areas without touching
upon any political matters. The Society is composed of
the following departments :-
Transportation
Relief
General Affairs

Secretariat

at present; it is expected that a certain amount of
revenue will be available when the Transportation
Department begins functioning. At present some 20 staff
members are employed in the office. All Society matters
are settled with the Japanese Consulate through a
Japanese adviser to the Society, a Mr. Jutaro Aiuchi who
has connections with the Japanese Consulate and both
military and naval authorities. Mr. Jutaro Aiuchi is
manager of the Shanghai Branch Office of Daido Shokusan Co.,
Ltd., No. Albury Lane, Chapee Road.
The names of the committee members of the society
are attached. The first mentioned nine persons serve
on the standing committee, three of whom, Messrs Koo Shing

TRANSLATION OF FRENCH POLICE REPORT NO. 2194/S DATED 24.1.38.

SUBJECT: Shanghai Citizens' Federation.
(上海市民协会).
（印：CONFIDENTIAL）

Soon after the occupation of the Shanghai area
by their troops, the Japanese Military Authorities
seriously considered the administrative reorganisation
of the conquered zone in the hope of re-establishing
normal conditions there.

In order to attain their object, they planned to
first create a Peace Commission similar to those already
established in several areas in North China, which,
under the direction of many well-known local Chinese,
have headed the work of reorganisation in occupied
territories and have acted as go-betweens between the
Japanese authorities and the population.

In the search for well-to-do Chinese necessary
for the successful realisation of the scheme, the
Japanese authorities naturally turned towards those
industrialists whose large interests in Chinese
territory were most susceptible of being compromised
by the duration of hostilities.

Thus, in this state of mind, a Japanese banker,
Mr. Jutarō AIUCHI, manager of the "Daido Industrial
Trading Company," 3 Albury Lane, Chapoo Road, approached
in mid-December, 1937, through the good offices of Mr.
CHOW WEN SUI, comprador of the Bank of Taiwan, 16 The
Bund, (residing at 4 Avenue Road), the following
individuals:

YAO MO LIE (姚慕莲), Managing Director of the
Nantao Waterworks, residing at 1033 Avenue
Joffre, 3rd. Floor of the Tower Building.
page_data.zh:
1938年1月24日法国警方第2194/S号报告译文。

主题：上海市民协会。
（上海市民协会）。
（印：机密）

日军占领上海地区后不久，日本军方当局认真考虑了对征服区的行政重组，希望在那里恢复常态。

为了实现这一目标，他们计划首先建立一个和平委员会，类似于已在华北几个地区建立的委员会，这些委员会在许多当地知名中国人的领导下，主导了占领区的重组工作，并充当日本当局与民众之间的中间人。

在寻找成功实施该计划所需的富裕中国人时，日本当局自然转向那些在华拥有巨大利益、且最容易因敌对行动持续而受损的实业家。

因此，在这种心态下，一位日本银行家、乍浦路阿尔伯里弄3号“大同产业贸易公司”经理相内寿太郎（Jutarō AIUCHI）先生，于1937年12月中旬，通过外滩16号台湾银行华经理周文瑞（CHOW WEN SUI）先生（居住于爱文义路4号）的斡旋，接触了以下人士：

姚慕莲（YAO MO LIE），南市自来水公司总经理，居住于霞飞路1033号，塔楼三楼。

page_data.en:
2

owner of several filatures and flour

此外，还决定任命前九名成员为联合会常务委员会委员，而其余成员将负责领导联合会在各区开展“重建”工作的各部门——即：

page_data.en:
4
Pootung          Messrs. CHEN TSE SHING & PAN TSE WEN
Chapei           ,Messrs. WA G PING YIEN & SENG TIEN SING
Nantao           Mr. YAO MOW LIE
Shanghai Western Area   Mr. YANG FOH YUEN
(Outside Roads)

It was also decided to notify the Shanghai Municipal
Council and the French Municipality of the creation of the
new organisation.

In accordance with the last decision the Federation
despatched letters to the two Muncipalities, to the Japanese
Ambassador in China and to the Japanese Naval High Command in
Shanghai informing these bodies and persons of its existence.

In thus endeavouring to create in Shanghai a federation
of Chinese citizens, it is certain that the Japanese authorities
sought to launch a movement for the organisation of a group
upon which they could rely for the realisation of their
schemes.    Although the Federation took care care to mention
in Article 1 of its statutes that it was not concerned with
politics and that its only programme was the re-establishing
of commercial and industrial affairs in the Shanghai region,
there remains little doubt that its creation has undeniable
political characteristics.

An analysis of its statutes shows, in effect, that
its real object is to quicken the return to normal conditions
of the Japanese occupied zone.    This is confirmed by the
fact that the Federation under the cover of busying itself with
charitable works, was considering the registration of
regugees desirous of returning to their own homes in the
occupied areas.    On the other hand, the presence of foreign
advisers (who can be only Japanese), as allowed for in the
statutes, indicates quite clearly that the entire question is
one bound up with Sino-Japanese cooperation.

The development of the new Federation which seemed
well on the way to success at the end of last month, now
appears to have been compromised by the assassination of
Mr. LOH PAH HONG (December 30, 1937) and the murder of Mr.
page_data.zh:
4
浦东          陳子馨先生及潘子文先生
闸北          王彬彥先生及沈田華先生
南市          姚慕李先生
上海西区      楊福源先生
（越界筑路区）

还决定将新组织的成立通知上海工部局和法公董局。

根据最后这项决定，联合会致函两个公董局、日本驻华大使及日本海军上海最高指挥部，告知这些机构和个人其存在。

因此，试图在上海建立一个中国公民联合会，可以肯定的是，日本当局寻求发起一场运动，组织一个他们可以依赖以实现其计划的团体。尽管联合会在其章程第一条中谨慎地提到它不涉及政治，其唯一纲领是恢复上海地区的工商业事务，但其成立具有不可否认的政治特征，这一点几乎毫无疑问。

对其章程的分析表明，其真实目的是加速日占区恢复正常状态。联合会以从事慈善工作为掩护，考虑登记希望返回占领区家园的难民，这一事实证实了上述观点。另一方面，章程允许聘请外国顾问（只能是日本人），这清楚地表明整个问题与中日合作紧密相关。

上个月底似乎进展顺利的新联合会的发展，现在似乎因陸伯鴻先生（1937年12月30日）被暗杀和杨福源先生

page_data.en:
5

YANG FOH YUEN (January 21, 1938). The result of these
terroristic acts has been the intimidation of the promoters
of the Federation and the postponing, sine die, of the official
inauguration of the group. Certain of the leading members
have been beset with fear: during the early days of January
Messrs. SENG TIEN SING, WANG YU CHING and HAN CHENG POU
published a notice in the vernacular pressstating that they
were not connected with the Federation. According to our
information, Messrs. WANG HSI FANG, MA CHI LIANG and YAO
SHING TSE desired to imitate their colleagues and only
gave up their intentions after intervention on the part of
Mr. CHOW WEN SIN, the medium between the Japanese authorities
and the Federation. Despite public denials, it is quite
certain that all the members of the Standing Committee
affixed their seals to the communications addressed to the
Municipalities soliciting registration and acknowledgement of
the Federation.

Thus, as a result of the assassination of Mr. LOH
PAH HONG and the murder of Mr. YANG FOH YUEN, the organisation
and affairs of the Citizens' Federation have come to a full
stop. Further, two of the principal organisers YAO MOA LIE
and YONG CHUNG CHING recently left Shanghai for Hongkong for
safety.

It is possible that the fruits of the scheme will
be taken up again in the future, but for the moment the
Federation exists only in name and has not been active
for some time now.

Attached herewith is a translation of the statutes
of the Federation.

（1938年1月21日）被谋杀而受到损害。这些恐怖行为的结果是恐吓了联合会的发起人，并无限期推迟了该团体的正式就职。某些主要领导成员感到恐惧：1月初，沈田華、王禹卿和韓承溥先生在中文报刊上发表声明，称他们与联合会无关。据我们了解，汪錫藩、馬季良和姚行之先生曾希望效仿他们的同事，但在作为日本当局与联合会之间中间人的周文瑞先生干预后，才放弃了这一意图。尽管公开否认，但可以肯定的是，所有常务委员会成员都在致函各公董局请求注册和承认联合会的信件上盖了章。

因此，由于陸伯鴻先生被暗杀和杨福源先生被谋杀，市民联合会的组织和事务已完全停滞。此外，两名主要组织者姚慕李和榮宗敬最近为安全起见离开上海前往香港。

该计划的成果将来可能会重新启动，但目前联合会仅存其名，已有一段时间未开展活动。

随函附上联合会章程的译文。

page_data.en:
TRANSLATION

STATUTES OF THE SHANGHAI CITIZENS' FEDERATION

Article I - This Federation has for its object the mutual
collaboration of the people and has no political character.
Its headquarters will be established in Shanghai and it
will be known as the "Shanghai Citizens' Federation.

Article II - In order to assist the residents of all
Shanghai and to remedy the present state of affairs,
the main offices of the Federation will be located
in one of the two Concessions and the branch offices in
Nantao, Chapei, Pootung, Eastern Shanghai and Western
Shanghai. In addition, if the need arises, branches will
also be established in other districts.

Article III - All Shanghai residents, of good conduct and
being legitimately employed, may become members of the
Federation.

Article IV - At the head of the Federation there will be
21 members (Committee Members), who will elect from among
themselves 9 members to form the Standing Committee. The
latter, in turn, will elect 3 of their number who will
form the Praesidium. The Praesidium will look after the
Federation's affairs whilst acting in uniformity with
Committee members. In the event of a branch being
created in another district, the main office will send
there several representatives who will co-operate with
the residents of that district; this branch must follow
all instructions given by the head office, which will
cause enquiries to be made vis-a-vis the functioning of
the said branch.

Should the branch not function well, the
head office has the right to recall its representatives
and to dissolve the branch.

Article V - The Federation may invite personages of any
nationality, Chinese of foreign, to act as advisers.

Article VI - The duties to be carried out by the Federation
will be the following:

1. To see that farmers, business men and workers
resume their affairs.

2. To reestablish communications between Shanghai
and other localities.

3. To make arrangements for entry into Shanghai of
foodstuffs, coal, cotton, etc.......

4. To develop reconstruction works.

5. To ensure sufficient work for the coolie classes.

6. To be able to obtain various products in different
districts.

7. To accomplish all charitable and aid works.

译文

上海市民联合会章程

第一条 - 本联合会以民众互助合作为宗旨，不具有政治性质。总会设在上海，定名为“上海市民联合会”。

第二条 - 为协助上海全体居民并补救当前局势，联合会总办事处将设在两租界之一，分部设在南市、闸北、浦东、上海东部和上海西部。此外，如有需要，还将在其他地区设立分部。

第三条 - 所有品行端正且有正当职业的上海居民，均可成为联合会会员。

第四条 - 联合会设委员21人，由其中选举9人组成常务委员会。常务委员会再从中选举3人组成主席团。主席团在与委员保持一致的情况下处理联合会事务。若在其他地区设立分部，总办事处将派遣数名代表前往，与该区居民合作；该分部必须遵循总办事处的所有指令，总办事处将对所述分部的运作情况进行调查。

如果分部运作不善，总办事处有权召回其代表并解散该分部。

第五条 - 联合会可邀请任何国籍的人士，无论是中国人还是外国人，担任顾问。

第六条 - 联合会应履行的职责如下：

1. 确保农民、商人和工人恢复其业务。

2. 恢复上海与其他地方之间的交通。

3. 安排粮食、煤炭、棉花等物资进入上海。

4. 开展重建工作。

5. 确保苦力阶层有足够的工作。

6. 能够在不同地区获得各种产品。

7. 完成所有慈善和援助工作。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No. ....................
S.1, Special Branch, SHANGHAI
REPORT
Date January 24, 1938.

Subject ......... Assassination in French Concession of Mr. Yang Foh Yuen,
reported to be concerned in the organization of the
Shanghai Citizens' Society

Made by D.I. Pan Lien-pih    Forwarded by C. Crawford. D.S.

At 3.50 p.m. January 21, 1938, Mr. Yang Foh Yuen
(楊福源) alias Yang Sing Tsung (楊心長), aged 48,
native of Shanghai, a prominent person in the Zao Woo
Kying Village, was shot and killed by an unknown assailant
outside the Tsing Zung Lee (親仁里), off Avenue Haig,
O.C.L. Yang lived with his family in house No.22 of the
above alleyway. The assailant, who is reported to be a
youth aged about 30, was wearing short jacket and pants
and a foreign overcoat, hair cropped short, and made good
his escape. The pistol used was found nearby the scene.
The deceased was the Commander of the Zao Woo
Kying Merchants Volunteer Corps and a follower of Huang
Ching Yung, a well known loafer in Shanghai. It is
reported that the deceased was once approached by
representatives of the Japanese Authorities, who asked
him to organize a "Peace Maintenance Society" at Zao Woo
Kying which he agreed to do, but he failed to make any
preparations. He was also reported to have been concerned
in the attempted organization of the Shanghai Citizens'
Society and to have been appointed Chief of Staff for the
rehabilitation of the Western District of Shanghai
(Vide Special Branch Report dated December 30, 1937).
Following the assassination of Mr. Loh Pah Hung (陸伯鴻),
one of the promoters of the Shanghai Citizens' Society,
it is reported that the deceased ceased his activities
towards supporting this Society.

Pan Lien-pih
D. I.
D.C. (Special Branch).

日期：1938年1月24日。

主题 ......... 法租界内杨福源先生遇刺案，
据报其参与组织上海市民协会事宜

制作人：督察潘连璧    转呈人：副督察长 C. Crawford

1938年1月21日下午3时50分，杨福源（楊福源），别名杨心长（楊心長），48岁，上海本地人，系曹吴泾村（Zao Woo Kying Village）之知名人士，在海格路（Avenue Haig）旁亲仁里（Tsing Zung Lee）外被一名身份不明的袭击者枪杀。杨氏与其家人居住于上述弄堂22号。据报袭击者为一名约30岁的青年，身穿短夹克和长裤，外罩一件西式大衣，短发，作案后成功逃脱。作案所用之手枪在案发现场附近被发现。死者系曹吴泾商团义勇队队长，且为上海著名流氓黄景荣（Huang Ching Yung）之门徒。据报，日本当局代表曾接触死者，要求其于曹吴泾组织“维持和平会”，死者虽口头应允，但未做任何准备。另据报，死者亦参与企图组织上海市民协会，并被任命为上海西区复兴参谋长（参见1937年12月30日特科报告）。在上海市民协会发起人之一陆伯鸿（陸伯鴻）遇刺后，据报死者停止了支持该协会的活动。

潘连璧
督察
特科副督察长。

Reference memo. dated 20/1/38 by D.C. (Special Branch) referring to above, attached hereto, D.S.I. Logan and C.A. Loh Sih-kya interviewed Mr. Randall Gould, Editor of the Ta Mei Wan Pao (Morning Edition) and Mr. H.P. Mills, Publisher of the Hwa Mei Wan Pao (Morning Edition) on the afternoon of 21/1/38, in order to ascertain the source of the report on above manifesto which was published in these newspapers on 1/1/38. Neither of these gentlemen were able to furnish the desired information, each explaining that the members of their night staff responsible for the publication of the report were absent from their respective offices but that when they attended office on the night of 21/1/38, the matter would be enquired into and any information available transmitted to Headquarters on 22/1/38. On the morning of 22/1/38, the Hwa Mei Wan Pao supplied to S. 5, Special Branch, a letter, written on plain paper but bearing the chop of the Shanghai Municipality Various Public Bodies' Joint Office, which it was stated had been delivered at the office of the Hwa Mei Wan Pao by ordinary mail, which contained a report of the manifesto in question (attached hereto) as published on 1/1/38. No reply was received, however, from Mr. Gould of the Ta Mei Wan Pao with the result that D.S.I. 参照特科副督察长于1938年1月20日就上述事项发出的备忘录（附后），1938年1月21日下午，副督察长 Logan 与华探 A. Loh Sih-kya 会见了《大美晚报》（晨刊）编辑 Randall Gould 先生及《华美晚报》（晨刊）出版人 H.P. Mills 先生，以查明这两家报纸于1938年1月1日刊登的上述宣言报道的来源。两位先生均未能提供所需信息，各自解释称负责发布该报道的夜班职员当时不在各自的办公室，但表示当他们在1938年1月21日晚回到办公室时，将对此事进行调查，并于1938年1月22日将任何可获得的信息报送总部。1938年1月22日上午，《华美晚报》向特科 S. 5 提供了一封信函，该信写在普通纸上，但盖有“上海市各团体联合办事处”的印章，据称是通过普通邮件送达《华美晚报》办公室的，信中包含了1938年1月1日刊登的所谓宣言报道（附后）。然而，未收到《大美晚报》 Gould 先生的回复，因此副督察长 Logan 于1938年1月24日与其联系，Gould 先生解释说，其报纸于1938年1月1日刊登的报道是收到的一封通过普通邮件寄来的信件中的内容，该信件此后遗失或放错地方，但据其中方职员称，信上盖有“上海市民协会”的印章（此名称可推定为上述“上海市各团体联合办事处”印章的另一种解读）。

January 12, 38.

Associations alleged to have opposed the formation of
the Shanghai Citizens' Society.

In accordance with instructions of the D.C.
(Special Branch), enquiries were made and the following
information obtained regarding the six organizations which
are alleged to have opposed the formation of the Shanghai
Citizens' Society :-

1. The Chinese Chamber of Commerce

The Chinese Chamber of Commerce is at present
situated in Room 414, Chung Wei Bank Building, 16
Rue de la Porte du Nord. A number of principal members
of the committee, including Messrs. Wong Shio-lai
and Tu Yueh-sung, have left Shanghai and are now in
Hongkong, Hankow and other inland cities, while
remaining members seldom attend office. The affairs
of the Chamber are, however, being managed by the
following people :-

Mr. Hsu Chi-ching (徐寄庼), member of the Standing
Committee, who is Manager of the National
Commercial Bank, 230 Peking Road, and member
of the committee of the Chinese Ratepayers'
Association.

Mr. Tsau Ts-kung (曹志功), staff member in the
employ of the General Affairs Department of
the Chamber, who is also a committee member
of the 1st Special District Citizens'
Federation.

2. The 1st Special District Citizens' Federation

The 1st Special District Citizens' Federation,
which is situated at 545 Kiukiang Road, conducts at
present no other activities than that of refugee relief
work. The following four committee members of the
Federation are looking after the affairs of the
organization :-

Mr. Wong Chien-ngoh(王劍諤 ), lawyer with an office
at Lane 361, 8 Myburgh Road.
Mr. Hsu Ts-kung (徐志功 ), a staff member of the
Chinese Chamber of Commerce.

3. The Shanghai Citizens' Association
The Shanghai Citizens' Association, also known
as the Shanghai Civics Association, of which Mr. Tu
Yueh-sung is chairman, is located in Room 415, Chung
Wei Bank Building, 16 Rue de la Porte du Nord. The
association activities have almost ceased, apart from
refugee relief work. Mr. Hsu Tsai-zung (徐采臣 ),
member of the General Affairs Department, is handling
the association's affairs at present. Other members
at present in Shanghai include Mr. O.S. Liu, a well-known
industrialist, and Mr. Kwoh Zung (郭順 ), General
Manager of the Wing On Company.

4. The 2nd Special District Citizens' Federation
The 2nd Special District Citizens' Federation is
an organization composed of residents in the French
Concession and had an office formerly at No.434 Rue
Auguste Boppe, but ceased functioning not long after
the withdrawal of the Chinese troops from the Shanghai
neighbourhood. Among the former committee members
of the Federation is one Mr. Mao Yuis (毛□ ), lawyer
page_data.zh:
- 2 -
刘仲英（Liu Zoong-ying）先生，华人纳税会委员，
居住于亚尔培路（Yu Ya Ching Road）4号587弄。
张一（Chang Ih-zung）先生，联合会第二难民收容所所长，
天潼路30号615弄。
王剑谔（Wong Chien-ngoh）先生，律师，
事务所位于迈尔西爱路（Myburgh Road）8号361弄。
徐志功（Hsu Ts-kung）先生，上海总商会职员。

3. 上海市民协会
上海市民协会，亦称上海 civic 协会（Shanghai Civics Association），
由杜月笙任主席，位于北苏州路16号中汇银行大楼415室。
除难民救济工作外，该协会的活动几乎停止。
总务部委员徐采臣（Hsu Tsai-zung）先生目前正在处理协会事务。
目前在沪的其他成员包括知名实业家 O.S. Liu 先生，
以及永安公司总经理郭顺（Kwoh Zung）先生。

4. 第二特区市民联合会
第二特区市民联合会是由法租界居民组成的组织，
原办公室位于奥古斯特·博佩路（Rue Auguste Boppe）434号，
但在中国军队撤离上海地区后不久即停止运作。
联合会前委员中有一位毛□（Mao Yuis）先生，律师

page_data.en:
- 3 -
by profession and a committee member of the local
Tangpu, who is Secretary of the Refugee Relief Branch
of the Disaster Relief Federation of Shanghai Benevolent
Societies, Pootung Guild, 1454 Avenue Edward VII,
and he is responsible for all outstanding business
connected with the association.

5. The China Culture Building Society
The China Culture Building Society, which was
more or less a subsidiary organ of the Central Kuomintang
formerly with an office at 500 Rue Lafayette, ceased
functioning and removed to the interior in the early
part of November, 1937, when a change took place in
the local hostilities. Mr. Herman Liu, Principal
of the Shanghai University, is dealing with the
outstanding affairs of the Society.

6. The Shanghai Municipality Educational Association
The Shanghai Municipality Educational Association,
originally situated in the Public Recreation Ground,
260 Dah Chih Road, Nantao, removed to No.482 Rue Auguste
Doppe, after the commencement of local hostilities, and
dissolved following the withdrawal of the Chinese
troops from the Shanghai area.

Enquiries made from these organizations which
are still functioning, show that they have no knowledge
of any meeting or any manifesto being published opposing
the formation of the Shanghai Citizens' Society as
page_data.zh:
- 3 -
为业，系当地塘浦委员，
现任浦东同乡会（地址为爱多亚路1454号）
上海慈善团体联合救灾会难民救济分会秘书，
他负责处理与该协会有关的所有未决事务。

5. 中国文化事业建设社
中国文化事业建设社大致为前国民党中央的附属机构，
原办公室位于辣斐德路500号，
于1937年11月初战事变化时停止运作并迁往内地。
上海大学校长 Herman Liu 先生正在处理该社的未决事务。

6. 上海市教育会
上海市教育会原址位于南市大治路260号公共游乐场，
战事开始后迁至奥古斯特·多佩路（Rue Auguste Doppe）482号，
并在中国军队撤离上海地区后解散。

对这些仍在运作的组织进行的查询显示，它们不知晓
有任何会议或发布任何反对成立上海市民协会的宣言，正如

page_data.en:
- 4 -
mentioned in the newspaper report published in the Tai
Mei Wan Pao Morning Edition of January 1, 1938. They
further state that the report intimating that they had
taken part in the opposition to the formation of the
Shanghai Citizens' Society was also unfounded.

With reference to the article published in the
"Shanghai Godo" of January 7, 1938, stating that the
S.M.C. had taken steps to order the Chinese Chamber of
Commerce and those other organizations to publish a
formal notice in the press denying that they were opposed
to the formation of the Shanghai Citizens' Society,
enquiries made show that there is no truth in the report.
No such notice has been issued with regard to the Shanghai
Citizens' Society to the local press, but a statement was
made by a representative of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce
during an interview with a reporter disclaiming participation
in the matter. The statement was published in the Shen
Wan Pao of January 6, 1938.
page_data.zh:
- 4 -
1938年1月1日《大美晚报》晨刊新闻报道中所述。
它们进一步声明，暗示它们参与反对成立上海市民协会的报道
也是毫无根据的。

关于1938年1月7日《上海日报》（Shanghai Godo）刊登的文章，
称工部局已采取措施命令上海总商会及其他组织
在新闻界发布正式通告，否认其反对成立上海市民协会，
经查询，该报道不实。
并未就上海市民协会一事向本地新闻界发布此类通告，
但上海总商会代表在接受记者采访时发表声明，
否认参与此事。该声明刊登于1938年1月6日的《申晚报》。

page_data.en:
January 14, 1938.
General Labour Union - present status

The Shanghai General Labour Union (上海市总工会),
originally situated at 94 Mei Ka Loong, Nantao, removed
to No. 482 Rue Auguste Boppe, following the outbreak
of local hostilities, and subsequently ceased functioning.
The most influential members of the union, including
Mr. Chu Hsueh-fan (朱学范 ), Chairman, and Mr. Chow
Hsueh-siang (周学湘 ), Vice-Chairman, have been absent
from Shanghai since the withdrawal of the Chinese troops
from the Shanghai area. Among the other committee
members who are at present in Shanghai are Mr. Yih Ziang-
kao (葉翔皋 ), follower of Mr. Loh Ching-dz (陸京士 ),
and Mr. Yu Yao-chiu (余耀球 ), staff member of the
local Tangpu; the latter mentioned individual is
maintaining a communication address c/o the Taichang-
Kading-Paoshan Fellow Countrymen's Association, 12 Rue
du Consulat, in order to deal with unsettled business
connected with the union.
page_data.zh:
1938年1月14日。
总工会 - 现状

上海总工会（上海市总工会），
原址位于南市梅家弄94号，
战事爆发后迁至奥古斯特·博佩路482号，
随后停止运作。
工会最具影响力的成员，包括主席朱学范（Chu Hsueh-fan）先生
和副主席周学湘（Chow Hsueh-siang）先生，
自中国军队撤离上海地区以来一直不在上海。
目前在沪的其他委员包括陆京士（Loh Ching-dz）的门徒叶翔皋（Yih Ziang-kao）先生，
以及当地塘浦职员余耀球（Yu Yao-chiu）先生；
后者为了处理与工会有关的未决事务，
维持着一个通讯地址，代收处为领事馆路12号泰康嘉定宝山同乡会。

page_data.en:
January 18, 38.

Associations alleged to have opposed the formation
of the Shanghai Citizens' Society

Mr. Yih Ziang Kao (葉翔皋) and Mr. Yu Yao-chiu
(余耀球), committee members of now defunct General
Labour Union, who are still in Shanghai, have been
approached and information requested as to the movement
by them to oppose the formation of the Shanghai Citizens'
Society. Both denied having any interest in the
movement, adding that they had no desire at present to
meddle in political affairs, and had no knowledge of the
manifesto published in the newspaper that they had opposed
the so-called Society in conjunction with other bodies.

Enquiries made through the "Shanghai Godo"
elicits the information that a reporter of the newspaper
submitted the article which he took from the Chinese
newspapers and included the General Labour Union
although there was no mention made of it in these
newspapers.
page_data.zh:
1938年1月18日。

据称反对成立上海市民协会的各团体

目前仍居上海的已解散之上海总工会委员叶翔皋先生（Mr. Yih Ziang Kao）和余耀球先生（Mr. Yu Yao-chiu）已被接触，并被要求提供有关他们反对成立上海市民协会之运动的情报。两人均否认对该运动有任何兴趣，并补充说，他们目前无意干涉政治事务，且对报纸上刊登的声称他们与其他团体联合反对所谓协会的宣言毫不知情。

通过《上海神户报》（Shanghai Godo）进行的查询获悉，该报一名记者提交了其从中文报纸上摘录的文章，并在其中加入了上海总工会，尽管这些中文报纸并未提及该工会。

In accordance with instructions of the D.C.
(Special Branch), enquiries were made and the following
information obtained regarding the six organizations which
are alleged to have opposed the formation of the Shanghai
Citizens' Society :-

1. The Chinese Chamber of Commerce 上海市商會

The Chinese Chamber of Commerce is at present
situated in Room 414, Chung Wei Bank Building, 16
Rue de la Porte du Nord. A number of principal members
of the committee, including Messrs. Wong Shiao-lai
and Tu Yueh-sung, have left Shanghai and are now in
Hongkong, Hankow and other inland cities, while
remaining members seldom attend office. The affairs
of the Chamber are, however, being managed by the
following people :-

Mr. Hsu Chi-ching (徐寄), member of the Standing
Committee, who is Manager of the National
Commercial Bank, 230 Peking Road, and member
of the committee of the Chinese Ratepayers'
Association.

Mr. Zau Ts-kung (曹志功), staff member in the
employ of the General Affairs Department of
the Chamber, who is also a committee member
of the 1st Special District Citizens'
Federation.

The 1st Special District Citizens' Federation,
which is situated at 545 Kiukiang Road, conducts at
present no other activities than that of refugee relief
work. The following four committee members of the
Federation are looking after the affairs of the
organization :-

January 7, 1938. - 2-

THE S.I.C. AND THE CITIZENS' ASSOCIATION

The declaration published in the newspapers
on January 1 under the joint signature of the Shanghai
Chinese Chamber of Commerce, the Federation of the
Special Districts' Citizens' Associations and the General
Labour Union, opposing the establishment of the Citizens'
Association, created much sensation among the general
public. Taking a serious view of this, the S.I.C.
took steps to order the above named three associations
to publish in the newspapers a formal notice cancelling
the declaration and to place the three associations
hereafter under strict supervision.
page_data.zh:
1938年1月7日。 - 2-

上海市民协会与市民协会

1月1日在报纸上联合署名刊登的宣言，由上海总商会、特区市民协会联合会和总工会签署，反对成立市民协会，在公众中引起了极大轰动。鉴于事态严重，上海市民协会（S.I.C.）采取措施，命令上述三个协会在报纸上刊登正式通告撤销该宣言，并将这三个协会置于严格监管之下。

CIVIC ASSOCIATION IS
DISAPPROVED
Chinese Public Bodies
Opposed To New
Organization

Another discouraging factor in the
rehabilitation of Shanghai was seen
yesterday when it was reported that
leading Chinese public bodies here
had met and decided to disapprove
the organization of the Shanghai
Citizens' Civic Association, a pro-
posed Chinese non-political organi-
zation aiming at revival of business
and communication systems.
Since the assassination of Mr. Loh
Pa-hong, no committeemen had
turned up at its temporary office in
the Women's Bank, Nanking Road,
and the day of inauguration has
been indefinitely postponed.
According to the "Hwa Mei Wan
Pao," public bodies, including the
Shanghai Chinese Chamber of Com-
merce, Shanghai Civic Association,
an organization formerly headed by
Mr. Tu Yueh-sen who is not in
Shanghai, Shanghai General Labour
Union, and Shanghai College Pro-
fessors' Association jointly held a
meeting on Friday and decided not
to recognize the new association.
The meeting decided to issue a
manifesto opposing the new organi-
zation and to discourage those who
would participate in forming the as-
sociation. It was also decided that
a Joint Office of the Shanghai Public
Bodies should be organized.
page_data.zh:
39

市民协会遭
反对
中国公共团体
反对新
组织

昨日有报道称，本地主要中国公共团体开会决定不赞成组织上海市民协进会（Shanghai Citizens' Civic Association），这是一个旨在复兴商业和交通系统的拟议中的中国非政治组织，这被视为上海复苏过程中的另一个令人沮丧的因素。
自罗伯洪先生（Mr. Loh Pa-hong，音译）遇刺以来，其位于南京路女子银行的临时办公室再无委员出现，就职典礼之日已被无限期推迟。
据《华美晚报》报道，包括上海总商会、上海市民协会（一个以前由不在上海的杜月笙先生领导的组织）、上海总工会和上海大学教授协会在内的公共团体于周五联合举行会议，决定不承认该新协会。
会议决定发表一份反对新组织的宣言，并劝阻那些参与组建该协会的人。会议还决定组建上海公共团体联合办事处。

page_data.en:
107

Mr. Okamoto Asks S.M.C.
To Put More Japanese In
Police And Other Organs

ARMY MAY BE FORCED TO TAKE STEPS
IN SETTLEMENT TO FERRET OUT
ANTI-JAPANESE ELEMENTS

SUGGESTION IS MADE THAT COUNCIL
SHOULD CONTROL CHINESE GROUPS

Mr. Franklin Declines To Make Comment In View
Of Importance Of Proposals; Consul-General
Is Accompanied By Representatives

Several requests were presented yesterday by Mr. S.
Okamoto, the Japanese Consul-General, to Mr. C. S. Franklin,
the Chairman of the Shanghai Municipal Council, with regard
to the eradication of anti-Japanese activities in the International
Settlement and an increase of Japanese influence in both the
Municipal Police and various organs of the Council.

Mr. Okamoto told the Chairman that the Japanese Expedi-
tionary Force "might be compelled to take steps as occasion
requires" to ferret out anti-Japanese elements in the Inter-
national Settlement. The Consul-General further stated that
the Japanese authorities regarded the recurrence of anti-Japan-
ese incidents as the result of the "inefficiency" of the Council's
efforts to suppress the anti-Japanese elements.

The Japanese Expeditionary Force,
Mr. Okamoto said, is "constrained to
feel" that the Municipal authorities
"lack earnestness or ability" to meet
the Japanese demand for the sup-
pression of subversive elements.

Suggested Steps

The final report of the demarche
emphasized that Mr. Okamoto had
stated that the Japanese Expedition-
ary Force might be forced to extir-
pate the anti-Japanese groups from
the Settlement "thus making it a
safer place to live in."

Under these circumstances, the
official said, the Municipal Council
is requested to take "appropriate
measures" to eradicate the anti-
Japanese elements and to exercise
rigid control of anti-Japanese news-
papers. As an essential means of
achieving the desired objectives,
the Japanese authorities were re-
ported to have asked the Council to
take the following steps:

1.—Increase the number of Japan-
ese members of the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Police and raise their status
and authority; and

2.—Place Japanese in controlling
positions in all important organs of
the Municipal Council.

During the course of the inter-
view, Mr. Okamoto was said to have
called Mr. Franklin's attention to
the fact that in the Chinese news-
papers of January 1 opposition had
been declared to the formation of
the Shanghai Citizens' Federation by
the General Labour Union, the
Chinese Chamber of Commerce and
the Special Citizens' Federation.

Retraction Asked

These organizations, Mr. Okamoto
was said to have asserted, have long
been engaged in anti-Japanese agita-
tion. For this reason, it was stated
Mr. Okamoto requested that the
Council take "immediate steps" so
that these bodies would retract
their statement and advertise their
retraction in the press and that they
henceforth be kept under the "rigid
surveillance" of the Municipal
Council.

The Japanese authorities, Mr.
Okamoto further informed Mr.
Franklin, regarded the recent anti-
Japanese incidents in the Settle-
ment as "a matter of serious con-
cern and regret."

In view of the importance of the
proposals, Mr. Franklin made no
immediate reply, promising to
make a thorough study of the
matter.

During the interview, which was
held between 11 and 12.20 o'clock
in the morning, Mr. Okamoto was
accompanied by Colonel Sanetaka
Kusumoto, assistant military attache
to the Japanese Embassy in China;
Captain Risaburo Fujita, acting
naval attache, and Mr. Noritake
Yoshioka, Senior Japanese Consul.
Colonel Kusumoto and Capt.
Fujita represented General Iwane
Matsui and Vice-Admiral Kiyoshi
Hasegawa, respectively commanding
the land and naval forces here.

In addition to Mr. Franklin, the
Municipal Council was represented
by the Secretary-General, Mr.
Stirling Fessenden, Mr. G. G. Philips,
Secretary of the Council and Mr.
Harold Porter, the Vice-Chairman.

Questions Answered

A number of questions regarding
the representations were asked
during the course of the afternoon
press conference yesterday. It was
asked if the reference to a control
of anti-Japanese newspapers was
made in connection with any of
the foreign papers. The spokesman
replied that "we will have to leave
that to your own judgment."

In answer to another question,
the spokesman said that no pro-
tests had been made to the French
Municipal Council. He stated that
there had been no grounds for
lodging a protest with the Conces-
sion authorities, there being no
evidence to show that the murder of
Mr. Loh Pah-hong had any connec-
tion with his alleged participation
in the Shanghai Citizens' Federa-
tion.

冈本先生要求工部局
在警察及其他机构中
增加日本人

军方可能被迫在租界采取行动
以肃清反日分子

建议工部局应控制华人团体

富兰克林先生鉴于提议的重要性拒绝置评；总领事由代表陪同

昨日，日本总领事冈本 S. 先生（Mr. S. Okamoto）向上海工部局董事会主席 C. S. 富兰克林先生（Mr. C. S. Franklin）提出几项请求，涉及消除国际租界内的反日活动以及增加日本人在工部局警务处和工部局各机构中的影响力。

冈本先生告诉主席，日本远征军“可能被迫视情况需要”采取行动，以搜捕国际租界内的反日分子。总领事进一步表示，日本当局认为反日事件的再次发生是工部局在镇压反日分子方面努力“效率低下”的结果。

冈本先生说，日本远征军
“不得不感到”市政当局
“缺乏诚意或能力”来满足
日本方面镇压颠覆分子的
要求。

建议采取的步骤

此次外交行动的最终报告强调，冈本先生曾表示，日本远征军可能被迫从租界铲除反日团体，“从而使这里成为一个更安全的居住地”。

在这种情况下，这位官员说，请求工部局采取“适当措施”消除反日分子，并对反日报纸实行严格控制。据报道，作为实现预期目标的基本手段，日本当局要求工部局采取以下步骤：

1.—增加上海工部局警务处中的日本籍警员人数，并提高他们的地位和权威；以及

2.—在工部局所有重要机构中安排日本人担任控制性职位。

据说在会谈过程中，冈本先生提请富兰克林先生注意，1月1日的中文报纸上，总工会、总商会和特区市民联合会宣布反对成立上海市民联合会。

要求撤回

据说冈本先生断言，这些组织长期从事反日煽动活动。因此，据说冈本先生请求工部局采取“立即步骤”，使这些团体撤回其声明并在报上刊登撤回广告，并且此后将它们置于工部局的“严密监视”之下。

冈本先生进一步告知富兰克林先生，日本当局将租界内近期的反日事件视为“令人严重关切和遗憾的事”。

鉴于这些提议的重要性，富兰克林先生没有立即答复，承诺对此事进行彻底研究。

此次会谈于上午11点至12点20分之间举行，冈本先生由日本驻华大使馆助理武官楠本圣隆大佐（Colonel Sanetaka Kusumoto，音译）、代理海军武官藤田理三郎大尉（Captain Risaburo Fujita，音译）和日本高级领事吉冈则武先生（Mr. Noritake Yoshioka，音译）陪同。楠本大佐和藤田大尉分别代表在此指挥陆海军的松井石根将军（General Iwane Matsui）和长谷川清中将（Vice-Admiral Kiyoshi Hasegawa，音译）。

除富兰克林先生外，工部局方面由秘书长斯特林·费森登先生（Mr. Stirling Fessenden）、工部局秘书 G. G. 菲利普斯先生（Mr. G. G. Philips）和副主席哈罗德·波特先生（Mr. Harold Porter）代表。

问题解答

在昨日下午的新闻发布会上，有人就这些交涉提出了一些问题。有人问及提及控制反日报纸是否涉及任何外文报纸。发言人回答说：“我们将把这个问题留给你们自己判断。”

在回答另一个问题时，发言人表示，未向法公董局提出任何抗议。他表示，没有理由向租界当局提出抗议，因为没有证据表明罗伯洪先生（Mr. Loh Pah-hong，音译）的被杀与他涉嫌参与上海市民联合会有关。
