Japanese Ask For
More Participation
In Police, S.M.C.

Officials Issue Warning Expeditionary Force May
Be Compelled To Take Steps To Ferret Out
Anti-Japanese Elements Here

IMPORTANT POSTS ON POLICE FORCE AND
ADMINISTRATION OF COUNCIL WANTED

Japanese officials yesterday morning issued a warning to the
Shanghai Municipal Council that the Japanese Expeditionary Force may
be compelled to take steps, "as occasion requires," to ferret out anti-
Japanese elements in the International Settlement.
That such a warning had been served was announced at the Japanese
press conference last night by a spokesman of the Japanese embassy.
The occasion was a call paid upon Mr. Cornell S. Franklin, chairman
of the Shanghai Municipal Council, by Japanese Consul-General
Suemasa Okamoto, accompanied by Colonel Sanetaka Kusumoto, re-
presenting General Iwane Matsui; Captain Risaburo Fujita, acting Naval
Attache to the Japanese Embassy, representing Vice-Admiral Kiyoshi
Hasegawa, and Mr. Noritake Yoshioka, Senior Japanese Consul.
Besides Mr. Franklin, Mr. Stirling Fessenden, Secretary General of
the S.M.C., Mr. H. Porter, Vice-Chairman, and Mr. G. Godfrey Phillips,
Secretary, were present.
In addition to the warning con-
crete proposals for increased Japan-
ese participation in the activities of
the Shanghai Municipal Council
were presented to Mr. Franklin by
the Japanese Consul-General.
Closer Co-operation Suggested
While expressing appreciation of
the efforts made by the S.M.P. to
check the recurrence of anti-
Japanese incidents, Mr. Okamoto
suggested closer co-operation be-
tween the Council and the Japanese
authorities in combatting terrorism.
Such co-operation, Mr. Okamoto
is said to have emphasized, could
best be insured by the Council's
adoption of the proposals made by
the Japanese authorities which in-
cluded the increase of Japanese
members of the police force, and the
appointment of Japanese to import-
ant S.M.C. administrative posts.
During the call, Consul-General
Okamoto informed Mr. Franklin
that the Japanese authorities re-
garded the recurrence of anti-
Japanese incidents as the result of
the "inefficacy" of the Council's
efforts to suppress anti-Japanese
elements in the International Settle-
ment. Reference was made to the
bombings on New Year's day in
which one Japanese soldier was ser-
iously injured and four others
slightly wounded when bombs were
thrown by persons not yet appre-
hended into a group of Japanese
soldiers on a sight-seeing tour while
the party was passing the intersec-
tion of Fokien and Hankow Roads,
as well as the bombings on the same
day at Japanese mills in the western
district and the grenading of Japan-
ese soldiers from Soochow Creek
bridges a few days previously.
The Japanese Expeditionary
Force, Mr. Okamoto said, is "con-
strained to feel" that the Municipal
authorities "lack earnestness or
ability" to meet the Japanese de-
mand for the suppression of sub-
versive elements.
The Japanese Expeditionary Force,
the demarche emphasized, may be
forced to extirpate the anti-Japan-
ese groups from the Settlement,
"thus making it a safer place to
live in."

"Appropriate Measures" Wanted
Under these circumstances, the
aide memoire said, the Municipal
Council is requested to take "appro-
priate measures" to eradicate the
anti-Japanese elements and to ex-
ercise rigid control of anti-Japanese
newspapers.
As an essential means to achiev-
ing the desired objectives, the Jap-
anese authorities asked the Council
to take the following steps:
1. Increase the number of Japan-
ese members of the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Police, and raise their status
and authority.
2. Place Japanese in controlling
positions in all the important
organs of the Municipal Council.
During the course of the inter-
view, Mr. Okamoto called Mr.
Franklin's attention to the fact that
in the Chinese newspapers of
January 1, opposition had been de-
clared to the formation of the
Shanghai Citizens' Federation by
the General Labor Union, the Chin-
ese Chamber of Commerce and the
Special Citizens' Federation.
These organizations, Mr. Okamoto
asserted, have long been engaged in
anti-Japanese agitation.
For this reason, Mr. Okamoto re-
quested that the Council take "im-
mediate steps" so that these bodies:
1. Retract their statement and
advertise their retraction in the
press, and
2. Are hereafter kept under rigid
surveillance of the Municipal Coun-
cil.
The Japanese authorities, Mr.
Okamoto further informed Mr.
Franklin, regard the recent anti-
Japanese incidents in the Settle-
ment as a "matter of serious con-
cern and regret."
In view of the importance of the
proposals, Mr. Franklin made no
immediate reply, promising to make
a thorough study of the matter.

日本要求更多参与
工部局警务处

官员发出警告：远征军可能
被迫采取措施以肃清此地之
反日分子

谋求在警队及
工部局行政中担任要职

日本官员于昨日上午向上海公共租界工部局发出警告，称日本远征军可能“视情况需要”被迫采取措施，以搜捕国际租界内的反日分子。
日本大使馆发言人在昨晚的新闻发布会上宣布已发出此警告。
此次警告的背景是，日本总领事冈本季正（Suemasa Okamoto）拜会了上海公共租界工部局董事会主席康奈尔·S·富兰克林（Cornell S. Franklin）先生，陪同人员包括代表松井石根（Iwane Matsui）将军的楠本实隆（Sanetaka Kusumoto）大佐、代表长谷川清（Kiyoshi Hasegawa）海军中将的日本大使馆代理海军武官藤田理三郎（Risaburo Fujita）上尉，以及日本高级领事吉冈典武（Noritake Yoshioka）先生。
除富兰克林先生外，出席者还有工部局总办费信惇（Stirling Fessenden）先生、副董事长H·波特（H. Porter）先生以及秘书G·戈弗雷·菲利普斯（G. Godfrey Phillips）先生。
除了发出警告外，日本总领事还向富兰克林先生提交了关于增加日本人在上海公共租界工部局活动中参与度的具体提案。

建议加强合作
冈本先生在表达对工部局警务处为遏制反日事件再次发生所作努力的赞赏之余，建议工部局与日本当局在打击恐怖主义方面进行更密切的合作。
据称，冈本先生强调，通过工部局采纳日本当局提出的提案，可以最好地确保这种合作，这些提案包括增加警队中的日本籍成员，并任命日本人担任工部局的重要行政职务。
在会谈期间，冈本总领事告知富兰克林先生，日本当局认为反日事件的再次发生，是由于工部局在压制国际租界内反日分子方面的努力“无效”。
文中提及元旦发生的爆炸案，当时身份不明的袭击者向途经福建路与汉口路交叉口的日本士兵观光团投掷炸弹，致使一名日本士兵重伤，另外四人轻伤；此外还提及同日发生在西区日本工厂的爆炸案，以及数日前从苏州河桥梁上向日本士兵投掷手榴弹的事件。
冈本先生称，日本远征军“不得不感到”，市政当局在满足日本镇压颠覆分子的要求方面“缺乏诚意或能力”。
此次外交行动强调，日本远征军可能被迫从租界内铲除反日团体，“从而使这里成为一个更安全的居住地”。

要求采取“适当措施”
备忘录称，在这种情况下，请工部局采取“适当措施”根除反日分子，并对反日报刊实行严格控制。
作为实现预期目标的基本手段，日本当局要求工部局采取以下步骤：
1. 增加上海公共租界警务处的日本籍成员人数，并提高其地位和职权。
2. 在工部局所有重要机构中安排日本人担任控制性职位。
在会谈过程中，冈本先生提请富兰克林先生注意，在1月1日的中文报纸上，总工会、中华总商会和特别市民联合会宣布反对成立上海市民联合会。
冈本先生断言，这些组织长期以来一直从事反日煽动活动。
因此，冈本先生请求工部局采取“立即步骤”，使这些团体：
1. 撤回其声明并在报刊上刊登撤回启事，以及
2. 此后受到工部局的严密监视。
冈本先生进一步告知富兰克林先生，日本当局将租界内最近发生的反日事件视为“令人严重关切和遗憾之事”。
鉴于这些提案的重要性，富兰克林先生未作即时答复，承诺将对此事进行彻底研究。

To Mei Wan Pao Morning Edition and other local newspapers.

SHANGHAI CITIZENS' SOCIETY.

At 2 p.m. yesterday a joint meeting was held by
a number of responsible members of the Shanghai Chinese
Chamber of Commerce, the Shanghai District Association, the
Shanghai Educational Association, the China Cultural
Reconstruction Association, the First and Second Special
District Citizens' Federations, etc.
The meeting was called to discuss the reported
formation of a "Shanghai Citizens' Society.
During the meeting the view was unanimous that
the proposed organization is an illegal body and the opinion
was held that most of the members of the Society had rendered
meritorious service in the past therefore they will never be
so reckless as to assume the "puppet" posts. It is presumed
that this body is being promoted by certain unscrupulous
elements for the furtherance of their own interests.
Moreover, the duties that this new body will perform, as
mentioned in local press reports, are not duties which
people are in a position to perform after the war.
As regards its propaganda for relief and other charitable
work, there are already in existence in this locality such
organizations which have all done good work.
The meeting expressed the opinion that such a body
as the proposed society was not necessary.
The following resolutions were discussed and
passed at the meeting:-
(I) That a manifesto be issued opposing recognition
of the Shanghai Citizens Society.

（印：SPECIAL BRANCH）

上海市民社。

昨日下午二时，上海中华总商会、上海特区协会、上海教育协会、中国文化重建协会、第一及第二特别区市民联合会等机构的若干负责人举行联席会议。
会议旨在讨论有关成立“上海市民社”的报道。
会上观点一致，认为拟议中的组织是一个非法团体，并认为该社大多数成员过去曾立下功劳，因此绝不会如此轻率地接受“傀儡”职位。据推测，该团体是由某些不法分子为推动自身利益而促成的。
此外，正如本地媒体报道所述，这个新团体将要履行的职责，并非人们在战后有能力履行的职责。
至于其关于救济和其他慈善工作的宣传，本地已有此类组织，且均工作良好。
会议表示意见，认为拟议中的社团这类团体并无必要。
会议讨论并通过了以下决议：-
(I) 发表宣言，反对承认上海市民社。

(3) That the members of the Society whose

(4) That a joint office of the various

Though the authorities of the Foreign
Settlements are intensifying their investigations into
the assassination of Mr. Loh Pah-hong (陸伯鴻), his
death will anyway affect the acceleration of the work of
the Shanghai Citizens' Society that was formed by leading
local merchants. Though certain responsible members of
the Society deny that the murder of Mr. Loh has had any
connection with the formation of this Society, yet they
are unable to assure definitely that it was entirely
unrelated to this affair. For this reason, the various
members of the Society, though they appear quite sincere
in their motives when interviewed by others, have given
indications of fear that their views might be misunderstood
by the public.
Following the publication by local papers
of the list of members of the Society, many of them have
denied any connection with the Society. Messrs. Sung
Di-sing (沈田莘) and Wong Yu-ching (王禹卿) deny any
participation in the Society. Mr. Lu Ngoh-zee (呂岳泉)
has declared that he is entirely ignorant of the fact that
he has been elected a member of the Society though he had
taken part in certain discussion for the formation of this
organization. Messrs. Chen Ts-ching (陳子馨) and Pan
Ts-vung (潘子文), members of the Board of Directors of
the Pootung Commercial & Savings Bank, state that they
have no knowledge that they had been elected members of
the Society and emphasized that the Society has nothing
to do with the bank itself.
In view of all these developments that
took place yesterday, it may be assumed that the Society
has met with a serious obstruction.

The "Ta Mei Wan Pao Morning Edition" of
to-day publishes the following letter from Mr. Yoong
Tsoong-ching (榮宗敬), a local Chinese cotton and flour
magnate:-
"In your morning issue of December 31,
there is published an interview with me on the subject of
the formation of a Shanghai Citizens' Society, but the
article is not correct. I have to make this important
announcement that our motive is purely to provide relief
for war sufferers. I have never said, as alleged, that
'there is practically no Government in China'. You are
asked to publish this letter as a correction in order to
avoid any misunderstanding."

随着本地报纸刊登该社成员名单，其中许多人否认与该社有任何关联。沈田莘（Sung Di-sing）先生和王禹卿（Wong Yu-ching）先生否认参与该社。吕岳泉（Lu Ngoh-zee）先生宣称，他对自己当选为该社成员一事完全不知情，尽管他曾参与过关于成立该组织的某些讨论。浦东商业储蓄银行董事陈子馨（Chen Ts-ching）先生和潘子文（Pan Ts-vung）先生表示，他们不知道自已已被选为该社成员，并强调该社与银行本身毫无关系。

REPORT
Date January 2, 1938
Subject Shanghai Citizens' Society - addresses of promoters.
Made by D.I. Pan Lien-pih Forwarded by C. Crawford

At 6.30 a.m., January 2, 1938, a hand grenade was thrown at 102 Avenue du Roi Albert, the home of Mr. Koo Shing Ih (顧馨一), Chairman of the Rice Hong Owners' Association and member of the Presidium of the Shanghai Citizens' Society, of which Mr. Loh Pah Hung (陸伯鴻), who was assassinated in French Concession on December 30, 1937, was also one of the leading figures. The grenade failed to explode. Simultaneously a number of coloured slips bearing inscriptions in Chinese "The U.S.S.R. has dispatched troops to fight Japan" were thrown into the compound and outside the door. A specimen of the slips is attached to this report. Mr. Koo's office address is the Yung Dah (永大) Cereal Hong, 8, Lane 25, Rue Montauban, French Concession, Telephone 85888.

The addresses of a number of the promoters of the Shanghai Citizens' Society, temporary office in Room 301, Shanghai Women's Bank Building, 480 Nanking Road (Tel.94140) (Vide Special Branch Report dated 30.12.37) have been ascertained and are given hereunder:-

Application of letter to Council
from the Shanghai Citizens'
Association.
Dated 19th December, 1937.

Rehabilitation Work

After the outbreak of the local hostilities on 15th August
most of the once prosperous business centres in Nantao, Chapei,
Pootung as well as in Western and Eastern Shanghai, were reduced
to ruins by either shells or fire. When fighting shifted west-
ward, all government and commercial organizations in that area
closed their doors. Two months have passed, but no rehabilita-
tion work has been taken in hand and the peace and order of the
community have not yet been restored. As a result an ever
increasing number of people have been rendered homeless and busi-
ness is only becoming more paralyzed. It is due only to the
protection afforded by the Council that residents in Chapei
are still able to eke out a precarious existence.

To allow Nantao and Chapei to remain in their present con-
dition is not a policy which can be pursued for any length of
time. In view of this the elder members of this community have
reached an agreement with the Japanese authorities on the or-
ganization by the undersigned of the Shanghai Citizens' Associa-
tion, whose functions it will be to undertake all rehabilitation
work for the various war-devastated areas. Survivors of the
hostilities will thus be able to return early to their accustomed
mode of living and the remaining financial resources of the
community be preserved. A copy of our Regulations is herewith
submitted for the Council's information. Please place this
matter on record and afford us assistance from time to time.

(Signed & Chopped)    Yung Tsung-ching
                      Yao Mo-lien
                      Ku Hsing-Ih

上海市民协会致工部局
信函申请。
日期：1937年12月19日。

复兴工作

自8月15日本地战事爆发以来，南市、闸北、浦东以及上海西区 and 东区曾经繁荣的商业中心大多被炮火或火灾夷为废墟。当战事向西转移时，该地区的所有政府和商业机构均闭门停业。两个月过去了，但复兴工作尚未着手，社区的和平与秩序也尚未恢复。因此，无家可归者日益增多，商业也愈发瘫痪。仅因工部局提供的保护，闸北居民才得以勉强维持艰难的生活。

让南市和闸北保持现状并非长久之策。鉴于此，本社区长老已与日本当局达成协议，由具名者组织上海市民协会，其职能是承担各战乱破坏区域的全面复兴工作。从而使战事幸存者能够早日回归惯常的生活方式，并保全社区剩余的财力资源。现附上本会章程副本供工部局知悉。请对此事予以备案，并不时给予我们协助。

Enclosure.
Regulations governing Shanghai Citizens' Association.

Art. 1. The object of this Association is to promote co-operation among the public. The Association is a non-political organization located in Shanghai under the title of "Shanghai Citizens' Association".

Art. 2. To meet the need of the general public in Shanghai for some form of voluntary effort to relieve the existing situation, this Association has been established with a main office in the Settlement with branches in Nantao, Chapei, Pootung, and in the Western and Eastern Districts. When necessary, additional branches may be extended to other localities.

Art. 3. All reputable residents engaged in lawful business in Shanghai are eligible for membership in the Association.

Art. 4. This Association shall have 21 Committee members. From among these persons, 9 shall be elected to form a Standing Committee, and from among the members of the Standing Committee three shall be elected to form a Presidium to conduct the affairs of the Association in conjunction with the other Committee members. When considering the question of establishing branches in other localities, this Association may co-operate with reputable residents in those localities, but such residents shall be subject to the guidance of the main Association.
Investigations shall be made from time to time. Should a branch of the Association be found inefficient in the administration of its affairs, the representatives sent by the main Association shall be withdrawn, and the branch abolished.

Art. 5. This Association may invite prominent Chinese and foreigners to serve as its advisers.

Art. 6. The functions of this Association shall be as follows:-
1. To restore agricultural, industrial and commercial activities.
2. To establish communication between Shanghai and other places.
3. To re-adjust transportation facilities so that there may be no shortage in the supply of food, fuel, drinking-water, cotton piece-goods, cotton and cotton yarn.
4. To promote building operations.
5. To maintain the business of porters, hawkers and labourers.
6. To revive various purchasing activities so that all commodities may be amply supplied.
7. To handle all matters relating to relief and charity.

Art. 7. All matters of this Association shall be decided on by the Standing Committee.

Art. 8. The detailed rules for the conduct of affairs of this Association shall be drawn up separately.

Art. 9. These Regulations shall be enforced after they have been approved by the Authorities.

上海市民协会章程。

第一条. 本协会旨在促进公众合作。本协会为位于上海的非政治性组织，名称为“上海市民协会”。

第二条. 为满足上海公众以某种形式的自愿努力来缓解当前局势的需求，特成立本协会，总办事处设在租界内，并在南市、闸北、浦东以及西区和东区设立分会。必要时，可将分会扩展至其他地区。

第三条. 凡在上海从事合法业务的信誉良好的居民，均有资格成为本协会会员。

第四条. 本协会设委员21人。从中选举9人组成常务委员会，并从常务委员中选举3人组成主席团，与其他委员共同处理协会事务。在考虑于其他地区设立分会时，本协会可与当地信誉良好的居民合作，但此类居民须受总会指导。
将不定期进行调查。若发现某分会管理事务效率低下，总会派出的代表将被撤回，该分会将被撤销。

第五条. 本协会可邀请中外知名人士担任顾问。

第六条. 本协会的职能如下：
1. 恢复农工商业活动。
2. 建立上海与其他地方的通讯联系。
3. 调整交通设施，以确保粮食、燃料、饮用水、棉布、棉花和棉纱的供应不致短缺。
4. 促进建筑工程。
5. 维持搬运工、小贩和劳工的生计。
6. 振兴各类采购活动，以确保商品供应充足。
7. 处理所有救济和慈善事宜。

第七条. 本协会所有事项均由常务委员会决定。

第八条. 本协会事务执行的详细规则另行制定。

第九条. 本章程经当局批准后施行。

December 31, 1937. Morning Translation

China Evening News of December 30 :-

SHANGHAI CITIZENS' SOCIETY : MR. YOONG TSOONG-CHING
INTERVIEWED

The inauguration of the Shanghai Citizens'
Society will take place soon. In the opinion of the
public this body is being looked upon as a sort of district
maintenance association.
Interviewed this morning by a reporter of this
paper, Mr. Yoong Tsoong-ching (荣宗敬), a member of the
presidium of the Society, made the following statement :-
"On the outbreak of hostilities in Shanghai, the residents
of Nantao, Chapei, Yangtszepoo, Hongkew and the suburbs of
Shanghai sought refuge in the International Settlement and
French Concession. Those who are poor were accommodated
in refugee camps, while others rented houses or sought
shelter with relations and friends. Five months have
elapsed, but the people are still homeless despite the
fact that the centre of military operations is now far
removed from Shanghai. In view of this state of affairs,
the authorities of the Foreign Settlements informally
expressed a hope that various Chinese bodies should endeavour
to bring about the early restoration of order in these areas,
whereupon certain commercial leaders began to work for a
revival of the market. In consequence, preparations were
begun for the formation of a Shanghai Citizens' Society to
undertake the rehabilitation work. After several
conferences, an agreement was drawn up and formally signed.
The various Councillors of the Shanghai Municipal Council
and the French Municipal Council will act as advisors to
this Society and assist in its work.
"The object of this body being as mentioned
above, its activities will have no connection with politics.
For the time being, the following will be its programme :-
"(1) An announcement will be published in the
newspapers that all bona-fide residents of Nantao, Chapei,
Eastern District, Eastern District, Woosung, Kiangwan and
Peoshan, who wish to return to their homes, may call, on
appointed dates, at the office of the Society to register.
No fee will be charged. If necessary, they will be required
to furnish proper securities, after which they will be issued
registration certificates permitting them to return to their
homes either for residence or for trade. In the meantime,
the authorities of the Foreign Settlements will open some of
the iron gates on the border of the Settlement and Chinese
controlled territory. Those who are in possession of
registration certificates will be regarded by the Japanese
authorities as law-abiding citizens and will not be inter-
fered with.
"(2) Inhabitants of various war zones will be
registered to permit them to return to their homes. All
inhabitants of war zones, such as Sungkiang, Soochow, Wusih,
Changchow, Kashing and Kiangyin, who are now living in the
Special Areas, may call at the Society and apply for
registration with guarantees. They will later be issued
with registration certificates which will permit them to
travel about without difficulty.

1937年12月31日。晨间翻译

12月30日《中国晚报》：

上海市民协会：采访荣宗敬先生

上海市民协会即将成立。公众视该机构为一种区域维持协会。
本报记者今晨采访了该协会主席团成员荣宗敬 (Yoong Tsoong-ching) 先生，他发表了以下声明：
“上海战事爆发后，南市、闸北、杨树浦、虹口及上海郊区的居民纷纷避难至国际租界和法租界。贫困者被安置在难民收容所，其他人则租房或投靠亲友。五个月过去了，尽管军事行动中心现已远离上海，但人们仍无家可归。鉴于此种情况，外国租界当局非正式地表示希望各华人团体努力促使这些地区早日恢复秩序，于是某些商界领袖开始致力于市场复苏。因此，开始筹备成立上海市民协会以承担复兴工作。经过多次会议，达成了协议并正式签署。上海公共租界工部局和法国公董局的各位董事将担任该协会的顾问并协助其工作。
“鉴于上述目标，该会的活动将与政治无关。目前的计划如下：
“(1) 将在报纸上发布公告，凡南市、闸北、东区、东区、吴淞、江湾和宝山希望返回家园的正派居民，可在指定日期前往协会办公室登记。不收取任何费用。如有必要，他们需提供适当的担保，之后将获发登记证，允许他们返回家园居住或经商。同时，外国租界当局将开放租界与中国控制领土边界上的一些铁门。持有登记证者将被日本当局视为守法公民，不受干扰。
“(2) 将对各战区居民进行登记，以便他们返回家园。目前居住在特别区内的松江、苏州、无锡、常州、嘉兴和江阴等战区的所有居民，均可前往协会申请带保登记。随后他们将获发登记证，凭此证可自由通行。”

Ta Hui Wan Pao Morning Edition :-

Other Interviews

In connection with the formation of the
Shanghai Citizens' Society, a reporter of the "China
Press" yesterday called upon Mr. Yoong Tsoong-ching,
a well-known industrialist, who lives in Seymour Road.
Mr. Yoong is one of the members of the presidium of the
Society.
According to Mr. Yoong, there is practically
speaking no government in China at present, therefore
the people need have no fear about undertaking any
movement that tends to alleviate their sufferings. He
emphasized that the new organization will have absolutely
no connection with the "Dah Dao City Government" nor
will it have any political affiliations. Its sole object
is to enable the refugees now being accommodated in the
Foreign Settlements of Shanghai to return to their homes
in Chapei or Nantao or Pootung or Woosung where they can
carry on their former occupations.
Mr. Yoong continued: "Personally, I belong
to no party; I am only a merchant. Business has come to
a complete standstill because of the hostilities. I
only hope that following the inauguration of the Society,
all industrialists who own factories in Chinese controlled
territory will be enabled to resume their business."
The Shanghai Citizens'-Society will have
the characteristics of a Chamber of Commerce or of a
District Association. It is a purely humanitarian
undertaking. It is being promoted and established by
leading local merchants. Its objects are:
(1) To make arrangements to permit refugees
to return to their homes and carry on their former
occupations.
(2) To enable factories located within the
zone of hostilities to resume operations.

“(3) 所有收容在外国租界内的难民将被遣返回其原籍。无家可归者将得到救济。
“(4) 将努力获取大米、食盐、燃料、蔬菜等日常必需品供应，以满足本地需求，从而压低物价，使贫民更易谋生。
该会的组建准备工作正在进行中，已在南京路的女界商业储蓄银行大楼租用了一处办公室。由于该办公室面积不够大，又在静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）爱文义路（Love Lane）附近的乡村俱乐部（Country Club）周边租用了一所房屋，将从12月31日起启用。目前，该会事务由顾馨一、姚慕莲、陆伯鸿（现已去世）、尤菊荪、王彬彦、陈子馨、周文瑞、祝伊才及本人处理。委员人数将会增加。登记工作预计在一周后开始。”

《大晚报》晨刊：-

其他采访

关于上海市民协会的成立，《字林西报》（China Press）的一名记者昨日拜访了居住在西摩路（Seymour Road）的著名实业家荣宗敬先生。荣先生是该会主席团成员之一。
据荣先生称，目前中国实际上没有政府，因此民众无需担心开展任何旨在减轻其苦难的运动。他强调，新组织与“大道市政府”绝对没有任何联系，也不会有任何政治派系关联。其唯一目的是使目前收容在上海外国租界内的难民能够返回闸北、南市、浦东或吴淞的家中，以便他们能继续从事以前的职业。
荣先生接着说：“我个人不属于任何党派；我只是一名商人。由于战事，商业已完全停滞。我只希望在协会成立后，所有在中国控制区拥有工厂的实业家都能恢复营业。”
上海市民协会将具有商会或同乡会的特征。这是一项纯粹的人道主义事业。它由当地主要商人推动和建立。其宗旨是：
(1) 安排难民返回家园并继续从事以前的职业。
(2) 使位于战区的工厂恢复运营。

December 31, 1937.

The suggestion for the formation of
this organization was informally made by the authorities
of the French Concession and the International
Settlement and was approved by the local Japanese
Consulate-General. Negotiations are at present in
progress with the Japanese Consulate.
In the opinion of Both Mr. Yoong and
other members of the presidium of the new organization,
such as Messrs. Yao Mo-lieh, Wong Ping-nyi and others,
the formation of such a new organization does not require
the permission of the Chinese Government. According to
Messrs. Yao and Wong, they have consulted the Chinese
Government over this matter but copies of the rules
of the new organization as well as of the manifesto on
its inauguration will be sent to the Government at
Hankow. In official documents, Mr. Wong said, the new
organization will still use the name of the Chinese
Republic and the national flag.
Mr. Yoong added: "There will absolutely
be no hope for the formation of the Society if the
permission of the Chinese Government has to be obtained.
We should be brave when undertaking anything that tends
to alleviate the sufferings of the people. We need have
no fear nor should we heed the consequences so
long as our motive is fair and just."
Later in the afternoon, the reporter of
the "China Press" paid a visit to the new office of
the Society at the Women's Commercial & Savings Bank
Building, No. 480 Nanking Road. According to Messrs.
Yao and Wong, they will not relax their efforts despite
the assassination of Mr. Loh Pah-hong.
They declared: "We will continue to
carry on our work and will not shift our responsibility
because of the death of Mr. Loh. The preparations are
now nearing completion. Letters requesting co-operation
from the authorities of both the International Settlement
and the French Concession have already been sent out."

Eastern Times and other local newspapers :-

Letters to the Two Foreign Councils

The following letter was sent to the
Shanghai Municipal Council and the French Municipal
Council yesterday by the Shanghai Citizens' Society:-
"As a result of the outbreak of hostilities
in Shanghai on August 13, most of the busy districts in
Nantso, Chapei, Pootung and the Western and Eastern
Districts have been destroyed. Although the fighting
has now moved to the West, no administrative and
commercial organs are functioning and no person has
emerged to restore order in these districts. It has
been only due to the good work undertaken by the two
Councils that the people of Shanghai are still able to
maintain their living.
"However, such conditions cannot be
allowed to continue. We are therefore making prepara-
tions to form a Shanghai Citizens' Society, the
organization of which is being promoted by local gentry

1937年12月31日。

组建该组织的建议是由法租界和国际租界当局非正式提出的，并得到了日本驻沪总领事馆的批准。目前正与日本领事馆进行谈判。
荣先生以及新组织主席团的其他成员，如姚慕莲、黄平夷等人认为，组建这样一个新组织不需要中国政府的许可。据姚先生和黄先生称，他们就此事咨询过中国政府，但新组织的章程副本以及成立宣言将发送给汉口政府。黄先生说，在官方文件中，新组织仍将使用中华民国国号和国旗。
荣先生补充说：“如果必须获得中国政府的许可，该会的成立就绝对没有希望。我们在从事任何旨在减轻人民苦难的事情时应该勇敢。只要我们的动机公正正义，我们就无需恐惧，也不必顾虑后果。”
当天下午晚些时候，《字林西报》的记者走访了该会在南京路480号女界商业储蓄银行大楼的新办公室。据姚先生和黄先生称，尽管陆伯鸿先生遇刺，他们不会放松努力。
他们声明：“我们将继续开展工作，不会因为陆先生的去世而推卸责任。准备工作现已接近完成。请求国际租界和法租界当局合作的信函已经发出。”

《申报》及其他本地报纸：-

致两个外国公董局的信

上海市民协会昨日向上海工部局和法国公董局发送了以下信件：-
“由于8月13日上海爆发战事，南市、闸北、浦东以及西区和大东区的大部分繁华地区已被摧毁。虽然战火现已向西转移，但这些地区的行政和商业机构均未运作，也没有人出来恢复秩序。上海市民之所以仍能维持生计，全靠两个公董局的良好工作。
“然而，这种情况不能允许持续下去。因此，我们正在准备组建上海市民协会，该组织由当地士绅推动

page_data.en:
December 31, 1937. Morning Translation.

and is approved by the Japanese authorities. As will be
seen from the rules of this Society (enclosed herewith),
the object of the Society is to undertake the rehabilitation
of the war-stricken districts so that the people may return
to their former occupations.
"You are requested to put our organization on
record and to render us assistance from time to time."

The Rules of the Society

The following are the rules of the Shanghai
Citizens' Society :-
1) This Society, to be known as the Shanghai
Citizens' Society, is formed at Shanghai for the purpose of
promoting mutual assistance among the people; it has no
political significance whatever.
2) This Society works for the relief of the
present situation as desired by the people of Shanghai.
For this purpose a Head Office has been established in
the Foreign Settlements of Shanghai and branch offices
will be established in Nantao, Chapei, Pootung, the
Western District and the Eastern District and at such
other places as may be necessary.
3) All law-abiding people engaged in proper
occupations in Shanghai may become members of this
Society.
4) This Society has an Executive Committee
of twenty-one persons. A Standing Committee of nine is
elected from among the twenty-one committeemen. A
presidium of three is elected from among members of the
Standing Committee. All affairs of the Society are
directed by the presidium and the Executive Committee.
The Society will co-operate with any law-abiding people
who desire to establish branch offices at their districts,
but all such branches must observe the directions of the
Head Office. Inquiries will be made from time to time.
If a branch office is being improperly directed,
the officials sent from the Head Office will be withdrawn
and the branch office will be abolished.
5) This Society may invite Chinese and
foreign notables to be advisors.
6) The work of this Society will be :-
(a) Revival of agriculture, industries and
commerce.
(b) Installation of communications between
Shanghai and other places.
(c) Obtaining of supplies of food, fuel,
water, cotton goods, etc.
(d) Development of building enterprises.
(e) Maintenance of manual labour, such as
porterage, hawking, etc.
(f) Purchase of various kinds of native
products from other places.
(g) Relief and benevolent works.
7) All affairs of this Society are directed
by the Standing Committee.
8) Regulations governing the works of this
Society will be drawn up separately.
9) These rules will be enforced after they
have been approved by the authorities.

并得到日本当局的批准。从本会章程（随函附上）可以看出，本会的宗旨是承担受灾地区的复兴工作，以便民众能够重返以前的职业。
“请贵方对本组织予以备案，并不时给予我们协助。”

本会章程

以下是上海市民协会的章程：-
1) 本会定名为上海市民协会，在上海成立，旨在促进民众互助；没有任何政治意义。
2) 本会致力于缓解上海民众所期望的当前局势。为此，在上海外国租界设立总会，并在南市、闸北、浦东、西区和大东区以及其他必要地点设立分会。
3) 所有在上海从事正当职业的守法人士均可成为本会会员。
4) 本会设执行委员会，由二十一人组成。从二十一名委员中选举九人组成常务委员会。从常务委员会成员中选举三人组成主席团。本会一切事务由主席团和执行委员会指导。本会将与任何希望在其辖区设立分会的守法人士合作，但所有此类分会必须遵守总会的指示。将不时进行检查。如果分会管理不当，总会派出的官员将被撤回，该分会将被撤销。
5) 本会可邀请中外名流担任顾问。
6) 本会的工作包括：-
(a) 振兴农工商业。
(b) 建立上海与其他地方的通讯联系。
(c) 获取食品、燃料、水、棉织品等物资供应。
(d) 发展建筑工程企业。
(e) 维持体力劳动就业，如搬运、叫卖等。
(f) 从其他地方采购各类土特产。
(g) 救济及慈善事业。
7) 本会一切事务由常务委员会指导。
8) 规范本会工作的条例将另行制定。
9) 本章程经当局批准后生效。

December 31, 1937. Morning Translation.

Meeting of Society

A meeting of all the committeemen of the
Society was held yesterday to discuss the question of
expenditure.
Mr. Wong Ping-nyi, one of the committeemen,
said: "According to the estimates, the expenditure will
not be very great. It has, therefore, been decided to
raise the amount necessary from among the committeemen and
the members. No contributions will be asked from the
public. Efforts will be made to obtain the use of some
public premises as offices of this Society free of charge."

Society Not Yet Inaugurated

The report that the Shanghai Citizens' Society
has already been inaugurated is denied by Mr. Yao Mo-lien,
Chairman of the Standing Committee. Mr. Yao stated that
questions of expenditure, office accommodation, rules,
etc., have not yet been settled, therefore the formal
inauguration of the Society cannot yet take place. He
also stated that the consent of Chinese and foreign
parties must first be obtained before the Society can be
inaugurated. After its inauguration, Mr. Yao added, the
Society will observe the directions of the Settlement
authorities. This Society has no political significance
whatsoever.

The following announcements appear in today's
issue of the "Sin Wan Pao" :-

Announcement of Mr. Wong Yu-ching (王禹卿)

In a report published by the "Ta Mei Wan Pao"
of December 30 on the formation of a Shanghai Citizens'

Owing to my poor qualifications and pressure
of business, I am taking no part in public organizations
whatever. I have nothing to do with the formation of a

This announcement is hereby published for

Announcement of Mr. Sung Di-sing (沈迪莘)

1937年12月31日。晨间译文。

协会会议

昨日召开了全体委员会议，讨论经费问题。
委员之一黄平夷先生说：“据估算，支出不会很大。因此，决定在委员和会员中筹集所需资金。不向公众募捐。将努力争取免费使用一些公共场所作为本会办公室。”

协会尚未正式成立

常务主席姚慕莲否认了上海市民协会已经正式成立的报道。姚先生表示，经费、办公场所、章程等问题尚未解决，因此协会尚不能正式成立。他还表示，必须先获得中外各方的同意，协会才能成立。姚先生补充说，成立后，本会将遵守租界当局的指示。本会没有任何政治意义。

今日《新闻报》刊登以下公告：-

王禹卿先生公告

在12月30日《大美晚报》关于组建上海市民协会的报道中，提到了我的名字。

December 31, 1937. Morning Translation.

Ta Mei Wan Pao Morning Edition and other local newspapers :-

MURDER OF MR. LOH PAH-HONG

Mr. Loh Pah-hong (陸伯鴻), a local Catholic leader, who is the General Manager of the Nantao Electricity & Tramway Company, is always zealous in charity affairs. Formerly he resided in Sz Ka Loong (史家弄), Nantao, but on the outbreak of hostilities in Shanghai, he removed to the 3rd floor of house No. 7, Lane 177, Avenue Dubail, French Concession, the house of a physician named Tsang Tseng-chia (莊振家), who is his brother-in-law.

At about 2 p.m. yesterday, three nuns called on Mr. Loh at this address and withdrew after 15 minutes, Mr. Loh seeing them off. After returning to his room, Mr. Loh instructed his chauffeur named Tsao Ts (曹子) to drive his private motor car (licence No. 992) to the mouth of the lane for he had to keep an engagement. Tsu Mei-pao (朱梅寶), native of Soochow, age 38, a relative of Mr. Loh, followed him as he intended to go to a certain place to meet friends. As Mr. Loh and his relative entered the car and the chauffeur was about to start the engine, two men in the vicinity of Dubail Apartments (杜拜公寓) who were dressed in blue jackets and trousers and disguised as orange hawkers, approached Mr. Loh's car, produced two pistols from the orange baskets and fired 12 shots at Mr. Loh. Three bullets penetrated Mr. Loh's breast near the heart and two struck him in the face. Mr. Loh collapsed in the car. The gunmen made good their escape. Mr. Loh's relative and his chauffeur, however, were uninjured.

Upon receipt of a report, a large party of Chinese and foreign detectives of the French Police arrived at the scene to make an investigation. Mr. Loh Pah-hong was removed to St. Mary's Hospital for treatment, but he succumbed soon afterwards.

At 4.45 p.m. yesterday, Mr. Loh's remains were removed by his family to the Shanghai Funeral Directors, Zi Ka Wei Road. It is learned that Mr. Loh will be encoffined at 2 p.m. January 2, 1938. The French Consul-General and Father Jacquinot yesterday visited the Funeral Directors to offer their condolence.

Detectives of the French Police found at the door of house No. 9, Lane 177, Avenue Dubail, a pistol, six inches long, which had been thrown away by the gunman and also many shells. This pistol is of German make known as "S Brand". The Police hold the opinion that the murder was premeditated and the motive is revenge. All officers have been instructed to conduct a strict investigation. The French Police offer a reward of $2,000 for information leading to the arrest of the gunmen. A photograph will be taken of the finger prints found on the pistol.

The motive of the murder of Mr. Loh Pah-hong is unknown. It is said that his death may probably have some connection with the formation of the Citizens' Society in this city.

1937年12月31日。晨间译文。

《大美晚报》早报版及其他本地报纸：-

陆伯鸿先生遇刺案

陆伯鸿先生（陸伯鴻），本地天主教领袖，兼任南市电气电车公司总经理，素来热心慈善事业。他原住于南市史家弄（Sz Ka Loong），但在上海战事爆发后，搬至法租界杜美路（Avenue Dubail）177弄7号三楼，即其姻兄弟庄振家医师（Tsang Tseng-chia）的寓所。

昨日下午2时许，三名修女前往该址拜访陆先生，15分钟后离去，陆先生亲自送别。回到房间后，陆先生吩咐名为曹子（Tsao Ts）的司机驾驶其私人汽车（牌照号992）至弄堂口，因他需赴约。朱梅宝（Tsu Mei-pao），苏州人，38岁，系陆先生亲属，随同前往，意欲去某地会友。当陆先生与其亲属进入车内，司机正欲发动引擎时，两名身穿蓝衣裤、伪装成橘子小贩的男子从杜拜公寓（Dubail Apartments）附近靠近陆先生的汽车，从装橘子的篮中取出两支手枪，向陆先生连开12枪。三颗子弹击中陆先生心脏附近的胸部，两颗击中面部。陆先生在车内倒下。枪手随即逃逸。然而，陆先生的亲属及其司机均未受伤。

接到报告后，大批华洋侦探赶赴现场进行调查。陆伯鸿先生被送往圣玛丽医院救治，但不久后身亡。

昨日下午4时45分，陆先生遗体由家属运往霞飞路上海殡仪馆。据悉，陆先生将于1938年1月2日下午2时入殓。法国总领事及饶家驹神父（Father Jacquinot）昨日曾前往殡仪馆吊唁。

法租界警务处侦探在杜美路177弄9号门口发现一支被枪手丢弃的六英寸长手枪及多枚弹壳。该手枪为德国制造，俗称“S牌”。警方认为此次谋杀系预谋作案，动机为复仇。已指令所有警官进行严密调查。法租界警务处悬赏2000美元，征集有助于逮捕枪手的情报。将对手枪上发现的指纹进行拍照留存。

陆伯鸿先生遇刺的动机尚不明确。据称，其死因可能与本市“市民协会”的成立有关。

新成立的“上海市民协会”将由21名主要成员组成，其中包括9名常务委员会委员。

常务委员会委员名单如下：-

Prominent local Chinese citizens, including Messrs.
Koo Shing Ih(顧馨一), Chairman of the Rice Hong Owners'
Association, Yoong Tsung Ching(榮宗敬), proprietor of a
number of Chinese cotton and flour mills in Shanghai and
Wusieh, Yao Moo Lien(姚慕蓮), a member of the gentry of
Nantao, Wong Ping Nien(王彬彥), Commander of the Chapei
Merchants Volunteer Corps, and Loh Pah Hung(陸伯鴻),
Director of the Nantao Electricity and Tramway Company, are
making preparations to form a "Shanghai Citizens' Society"
(上海市民協會), with a view to rehabilitating the
Shanghai area. They have at present established a temporary
office in Room 301 Shanghai Women's Bank Building, 480
Nanking Road.(Tel. 94140).

The promoters of the Society persistently maintain
that the organization should be independent from the
Japanese Military and Political Authorities, at least in name,
and have, after protracted negotiations, agreed to deal with
the latter in future through Mr. Jutaro Ainchi, Manager of
Daido Industrial Trading Company, No. 3 Albury Lane, Chapoo
Road, and concurrently, it is reported, an advisor to the
Japanese Military in Shanghai. Mr. Chow Wen Zueh(周文瑞),
Chinese compradore of the Bank of Taiwan, has been appointed
to assist Mr. Jutaro Ainchi in the liaison work.

Between 3 p.m. and 5.30 p.m. December 29, Mr. Jutaro
Ainchi and some twenty Chinese prominent local citizens,
including the following, held a meeting in Room 301 Shanghai
Women's Bank Building, No. 480 Nanking Road:-
Mr. Koo Shing Ih
Mr. Loh Pah Hung

本地知名华人公民，包括米业公会主席顾馨一先生（Koo Shing Ih）、在上海及无锡拥有多家华资棉纺厂和面粉厂的业主荣宗敬先生（Yoong Tsung Ching）、南市士绅姚慕莲先生（Yao Moo Lien）、闸北商团团长王彬彦先生（Wong Ping Nien）以及南市电气电车公司董事陆伯鸿先生（Loh Pah Hung），正筹备成立“上海市民协会”（上海市民協會），旨在复兴上海地区。他们目前在南京路480号上海女子银行大楼301室设立了临时办事处。（电话：94140）。

该协会发起人坚持认为，该组织至少在名义上应独立于日本军政当局，并经过长期谈判，同意今后通过大同工业贸易公司经理、据报同时担任驻沪日军顾问的爱知次郎（Jutaro Ainchi）先生与日方打交道，公司地址位于乍浦路阿尔伯里弄3号。台湾银行华买办周文瑞先生（Chow Wen Zueh）已被任命协助爱知次郎先生进行联络工作。

Mr. Yang Foh Yuen(楊福源), Commander of the Zao Woo
Kying Merchants volunteer Corps and a follower of
Hwang King Yoong, a well known loafer in Shanghai.
Mr. Jutaro Ainchi addressed the attendance in Japanese with
Chow Wen Zueh as interpretor, stating that it was a great
pity to see all business at a standstill, thereby embarrassing
the livelihood of the people. All being business men and
all having at heart the well being of kindred human beings,
it had been suggested to form this society. The attendance,
Mr. Jutaro Ainchi concluded, were urged to accelerate the
arrangements for the formation of the society for the
benefit of the public. Discussions were then made and the
following resolutions passed:-
1. That the S.M.C. and the C.M.F. be formally notified of
the formation of the Society prior to its inauguration.
